docs.title: Market Trading Guide: Adani Power among 2 stock recommendations for Friday
docs.text:
Indian equities rallied sharply on Thursday as concerns over stretched AI valuations and higher US inflation triggered a sell-off across tech-heavy global markets, improving India’s relative appeal and encouraging rotation toward domestic large-cap technology, private financials and defensive heavyweights. 
 Analysts say near-term sustainability will depend on Q2 earnings delivering on revenue and margins, broader market participation and evidence of returning foreign flows, while durable stability in oil and the currency remains crucial amid geopolitical and global inflation risks.
Here are 2 stock recommendations for Friday
 Buy Bajaj Holdings at Rs 11,220-11,225 | Stop loss: Rs 10,770 | Target: Rs 12,100 
Bajaj Holdings is showing a strong bullish recovery, with the latest session closing at ₹11,225, up 4.19%, supported by a strong bullish candle and improved buying momentum. The stock has moved above its key moving averages, indicating a potential improvement in the short-term trend. The RSI has rebounded sharply toward 57, crossing above the 50 mark and its signal line, suggesting strengthening bullish momentum without entering the overbought zone. Sustaining above ₹11,100 could support further upside toward recent resistance levels around Rs 11,900–12,100.
 Live Events
Virat Jagad, Sr. Technical Research Analyst, at Bonanza Portfolio Ltd
 Buy Adani Power at Rs 196-197 | Stop loss: Rs 188.5 | Target: Rs 212 
Adani Power is showing signs of a potential recovery after finding support near the Rs 185–190 zone, with the latest session closing at ₹196.50. The stock has witnessed a positive rebound from recent lows, indicating improving buying interest near its long-term moving average. The RSI has recovered from the oversold region toward the 45–50 zone, suggesting that bearish momentum is easing. A sustained move above Rs 200–205 could strengthen the recovery and open the possibility of further upside, while Rs 190 remains an important support zone.
Virat Jagad, Sr. Technical Research Analyst, at Bonanza Portfolio Ltd

docs.title: AI stock selloff eases as investors buy on dips amid falling bond yields
docs.text:
The selloff in some of the riskiest AI-linked stocks eased on Thursday as buyers returned to the technology sector following a weak US open, while falling bond yields reduced pressure on highly leveraged companies, Reuters reported.
 Data-centre operator CoreWeave remained in focus. Its shares fell 2% by midday after tumbling as much as 10% earlier in the session and plunging 15% on Wednesday. The company’s bonds traded at yields as high as 16%, while its credit-default swap spreads widened, underscoring concerns about rising financing costs. Wednesday’s hotter-than-expected US inflation report highlighted the risks that elevated borrowing costs posed to the capital-intensive AI sector.
 As on 16 Oct 2026, 01:11 AM IST
 S&P 500 Top Gainers
 Trade Desk 13.10 (7.51%) 
 Pool 169.36 (7.11%) 
 Coinbase Global 184.66 (6.81%) 
 Expedia Group 293.20 (6.74%) 
 Gainers » 
 S&P 500 Top Losers
 Coterra Energy 32.56 (-8.62%) 
 Dell Technologies 467.68 (-7.92%) 
 Hewlett Packard 59.07 (-6.40%) 
 Arista Networks 185.34 (-5.16%) 
 Losers » 
Selling remained concentrated among heavily indebted companies and stocks that had recorded substantial gains earlier this year. AI infrastructure provider Nebius fell 5%, AI server maker Dell Technologies dropped 7%, and memory-chip company SanDisk lost 2%. Despite the declines, Nebius had gained 112% in 2026, Dell had surged 273%, and SanDisk had climbed 476%, according to LSEG data.
 For live updates on US Markets, click here 
Some investors said an infrastructure expansion billed as the largest ever was inevitably likely to face setbacks. They expected further volatility as interest rates rose and expectations of additional Federal Reserve tightening increased.
 Live Events
“While increased competition within AI, rising financing requirements and higher rates may periodically add to volatility, we view this latest bout as more of a recalibration of expectations than a fundamental break in the AI investment story,” said Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi, chief investment officer for the Americas and global head of equities at the UBS Chief Investment Office.
 AI slowdown concerns
Concerns surrounding CoreWeave and similarly positioned companies partly reflected perceptions that growth had slowed at Anthropic and OpenAI, two major AI laboratories at the centre of the boom.
According to an investor who attended a meeting with Anthropic’s leadership in San Francisco on Wednesday, the company’s third-quarter revenue had risen 45% sequentially to $16.8 billion. Some analysts considered that figure disappointing given the sector’s lofty expectations and Anthropic’s reported pursuit of a $2 trillion valuation.
“We’re getting a whole lot of information suggesting that the largest AI companies may not be generating the earnings or revenue people anticipated, and I think that makes everyone nervous about companies like CoreWeave,” Kim Forrest, chief investment officer at Bokeh Capital Partners, told Reuters.
CoreWeave CEO Mike Intrator said in an internal memo that the market was acting “irrationally” and that he remained confident in the AI cloud company, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday.
 Also Read: Why are credit default swaps unnerving AI investors? 
Investors nevertheless remained broadly optimistic about the sector because its largest companies, including chip designer Nvidia and hyperscalers Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta and Amazon, were highly profitable and widely viewed as well-managed despite debt-related concerns.
However, higher interest rates were expected to increase borrowing and construction costs, with unprofitable and less-profitable companies likely to face the greatest pressure. US Treasury yields extended their recent decline on Thursday, with the 10-year yield briefly approaching 5% before moving higher again. Even so, elevated inflation had altered investors’ expectations for interest rates.
“I do think long rates above 5% and creeping towards 6% is a problem for the marginal borrower, I’ll call them,” said Ross Mayfield, investment strategy analyst at Baird. “It gets a lot harder for the tiers below the kind of big four hyperscalers.”
The Nasdaq was down 0.4% on Thursday afternoon, while Alphabet and most other hyperscalers were little changed. SpaceX, another major AI company, fell 3%.
“This select group of companies is driving most of the growth in the economy and the stock market, and they’re investing so, so aggressively and investors just aren’t really willing to pay for it or fully buy in to the extent that we saw in the late ’90s or whatever when investors kind of lost their minds,” said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management. “Investors have definitely not lost their minds. They’re being very cautious, and I think selective.”

docs.title: Ready for take-off? Analysts map the flight path for India's aerospace stocks
docs.text:
India’s aerospace sector is gearing up for a multi-year growth opportunity, driven by rising air travel, expanding aircraft production, higher defence expenditure and global aircraft manufacturers diversifying their supply chains.
 Government efforts to boost domestic manufacturing, coupled with India’s cost-competitive manufacturing base and skilled workforce, are creating opportunities across aircraft platforms, precision components, avionics and maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO), according to the All India Association of Industries.
Analysts, meanwhile, believe the sector is on a strong runway, poised for take-off, with rising aircraft production, export growth, new customer wins and MRO expansion emerging as key growth drivers.
 Analysts map the flight path
India’s aerospace sector is at an interesting juncture, with growth in aviation, global original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) expanding their Indian sourcing and a push towards defence indigenisation creating opportunities across precision manufacturing, avionics, aircraft platforms and MRO, said Vipin Singhal, director, Anand Rathi Investment Banking.
The key, however, is to look beyond order books, Singhal said.
 Live Events
“Aerospace qualification creates long-term customer relationships, but can also mean concentration risk. Revenue conversion, margins and cash flows will ultimately determine the quality of growth. With valuations factoring in much of the indigenisation and China+1 opportunity, execution will be critical. MRO is another segment worth watching for its potential to generate more recurring revenues,” he said.
Listed companies, he believes, offer different exposures to the opportunity. Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd (HAL), for instance, depends on programme execution and delivery schedules, while Data Patterns brings design and electronics capabilities, where proprietary technology matters.
 Azad Engineering and MTAR Technologies , meanwhile, are precision manufacturing plays, with growth linked to OEM approvals, programme ramp-ups and their non-aerospace businesses, Singhal said.
Echoing similar views, Putta Ravi Kumar, defence analyst at Choice Institutional Equities, said the sector is entering a multi-year growth cycle, supported by rising air travel, aircraft production and global OEMs diversifying their supply chains.
Precision component suppliers appear particularly well positioned to capture this opportunity, given India’s growing traction in aerospace manufacturing and supply-chain localisation, Kumar said.
Key triggers for the sector, according to Kumar, include rising aircraft production, export growth, new customer wins and MRO expansion. However, execution delays, customer concentration, capacity ramp-up challenges and elevated valuations remain key risks.
 ALSO READ: Rethink the short term, but it is only about business in the long term: 5 mid-cap stocks with upside potential of up to 23% 
 Which stocks are set to take off?
Among listed companies, Kumar is bullish on Unimech Aerospace & Manufacturing, citing its specialised capabilities in aero tooling and precision engineering.
As global aircraft production scales up, qualified Indian suppliers stand to benefit from higher outsourcing and localisation, he said. HAL also offers exposure to India’s domestic aircraft manufacturing opportunity.
“The opportunity is supported by a global aircraft backlog of more than 15,000 aircraft at Airbus and Boeing and India’s ambition to build a US$4 billion MRO industry by 2030. This creates a dual growth opportunity in precision components for new aircraft production and maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) as the fleet expands,” Kumar said.
“The bigger opportunity lies in identifying Indian suppliers with specialised capabilities and global customer approvals that can move up the aerospace value chain, not simply betting on rising air travel,” he said.

docs.title: Global Market: Bank of China (Hong Kong) plans $3.3 billion onshore yuan debt issuance
docs.text:
Bank of China (Hong Kong), the sole yuan-clearing bank in the financial hub, plans to issue up to 22.2 billion yuan ($3.3 billion) worth of interbank negotiable certificates of deposit (NCDs) in China's onshore market in 2026. This move aims to strengthen Hong Kong 's position as a leading offshore yuan centre, according to a report by Reuters.
 The lender has become the first offshore yuan-clearing bank to receive an issuance quota for onshore NCDs, according to a statement from China's Interest Rate Self-Regulatory Mechanism, which the People's Bank of China oversees, as per the report.
 As on 15 Oct 2026, 01:30 AM IST
 S&P 500 Top Gainers

 Gainers » 
 S&P 500 Top Losers

 Robinhood Markets 101.08 (-8.54%) 
 Losers » 
 Also Read | Global Market: Japan’s Nikkei plunges nearly 5% as AI stocks tumble on CoreWeave debt concerns 
The bank plans to denominate all the instruments in yuan and will determine the size and maturity of each issuance based on market conditions and its own financing requirements, according to a separate statement issued this week.
NCDs are short-term debt instruments banks commonly issue to meet financing needs. The planned issuance would give Bank of China (Hong Kong) access to another funding channel in mainland China, potentially strengthening financial links between the onshore and offshore yuan markets.
 Live Events
 Also Read | Global Market: China stocks fall as hot US inflation data revives rate hike fears 
The move comes as Beijing and Hong Kong intensify efforts to establish the city as a leading offshore yuan centre. In July, authorities from both sides unveiled a series of measures to boost currency, bond and gold trading in Hong Kong amid heightened geopolitical tensions.
Hong Kong plays a key role in China's efforts to internationalise the yuan by providing offshore liquidity and financial infrastructure for transactions in the currency. Expanding funding options for financial institutions in the city could further support yuan-denominated business and cross-border investment, the report stated.
The yield on one-year NCDs stood at around 1.44%, while the Hong Kong offshore yuan interbank offered rate (HIBOR), a benchmark for yuan borrowing costs in the city, was approximately 1.78% this week.
The planned issuance underscores efforts to deepen integration between mainland China's financial markets and Hong Kong's offshore yuan market, as authorities seek to expand the international use of the Chinese currency, as per the report.

docs.title: China's ByteDance sets up AI safety team, launches global hiring drive
docs.text:
Synopsis
 In a proactive move to address concerns surrounding artificial intelligence safety, ByteDance's AI research division, Seed, is assembling a dedicated Alignment & Preparedness team. The aim is to onboard 10 specialized researchers in Beijing, Shanghai, and San Jose. This initiative reflects the growing demand for robust AI capabilities and safety protocols in the U.S. and China.
 Listen to this article in summarized format
 Listen 
 Chinese tech giant ByteDance's AI research unit Seed has created an Alignment & Preparedness team and launched a global drive to recruit 10 researchers, saying it will make a long-term investment in AI safety for its increasingly capable models.
The hiring push comes as scrutiny of AI-agent safety grows in China and the US, especially as developers give them autonomy to access the Internet.
 AI alignment refers to efforts to ensure advanced AI systems act in line with human goals and safety requirements, particularly when carrying out complex, multi-step tasks. 
ByteDance's announcement is a rare public disclosure by a major Chinese AI developer of a dedicated effort focused on frontier-model safety, alignment and preparedness for emerging risks.
State-backed newspaper The Paper reported on Tuesday that Seed was the first Chinese frontier AI lab to establish a standalone safety and alignment department.
The move also comes amid broader US-China discussions on AI guardrails, safety risks and channels for communicating about major AI-related incidents, even as the two countries compete for leadership in advanced AI.
As model capabilities improve, safety and alignment are no longer simply safeguards against risk but core capabilities that will determine whether models can be deployed at scale, Seed said in a recruitment post published on its official WeChat account on Wednesday.
Seed said it would provide the new team with computing capacity and research resources comparable to those available to frontier-model teams. The positions are based in Beijing, Shanghai and San Jose, California.
Its research will include safety training across model-development stages, automated testing for vulnerabilities, tools to monitor and explain model behaviour, AI-agent testing environments and preparations for emerging risks.
Seed said it would also seek independent testing and work with universities and research institutions, applying safety research across model training, evaluation and deployment.

docs.title: Indian rice export prices hit over 1 year high on stronger rupee, crop supply concerns
docs.text:
Asian rice export prices in key hubs remained firm this week, with Indian rates hitting a more than one-year high on stronger rupee and crop supply concerns, while Vietnamese prices rose to a near two-month high on expectations of stronger demand.
 India's 5% broken parboiled variety was quoted at $384-$389 per ton this week, up from last week's $378-$384. Indian 5% broken white rice was priced at $385 to $390 per ton.
"Paddy prices remain firm in the domestic market due to limited supplies. Production has declined in several states because of below-normal rainfall," said a Mumbai-based exporter. 
Vietnam's 5% broken rice was offered at $440-$450 per metric ton on Thursday, its highest level since August 21, up from $420-$430 a week ago.
"We are told that the Philippines will resume rice purchases from Vietnam from November," a trader based in Ho Chi Minh City said.
 Live Events
A Vietnamese agriculture ministry official said this week that rice export activity is expected to be busy during the rest of this year, adding that the country's target to export 8 million tons of rice will be met.
In Thailand, 5% broken rice was quoted at $480 per ton, highest since September 10, up from $465 to $468 last week.
The arrival of vessels to collect rice shipments and additional purchases by some exporters pushed prices higher, a Bangkok-based rice trader said.
Flooding has delayed loading, while some exporters have had to buy additional rice as the off-season harvest nears its end, adding upward pressure on prices, the trader said.
Thailand's rice exports could fall short of this year's 7-million-ton target amid competition from India and Pakistan and weaker demand from major buyers, according to the Thai Rice Exporters Association.
In Bangladesh, rice prices rose over the past week, driven by higher fuel costs and rising paddy prices, with fine rice rising to 74-75 taka per kilogram from 72 taka a week earlier, adding to the financial strain on consumers already grappling with persistently high living costs.

 Abhijeet Dipke , founder of the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), once questioned an umpire's decision during a Virat Kohli innings that ended with the Indian batter scoring his 48th ODI century. Dipke also took aim at the International Cricket Council (ICC), describing it as a “toothless body” in front of the Board of Control for Cricket in India ( BCCI ). The remarks date back to October 19, 2023, when India played Bangladesh in the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup. Kohli was approaching his century during India's chase when a delivery from Bangladesh spinner Nasum Ahmed was not called wide by umpire Richard Kettleborough.
Dipke took to X to criticise the decision, alleging that the umpire had allowed Kohli to move closer to his personal milestone. He also referred to former Sri Lanka captain Arjuna Ranatunga's criticism of the ICC and its relationship with the BCCI. The old posts have resurfaced as Dipke attracts attention over his political activities and protests in Delhi. His earlier statements are now being shared and discussed on social media. 
— abhijeet_dipke (@abhijeet_dipke) 
 What did Abhijeet Dipke say about Virat Kohli?
Dipke posted his first criticism on X during the India-Bangladesh match on October 19, 2023. “Umpire refused to give a clear wide so Kohli can complete his century. Arjuna Ranatunga wasn’t wrong when he said that the ICC is a toothless body in front of the BCCI. Can’t have different set of rules for one specific team,” he wrote.
 Live Events
 You Might Also Like: 
 Imran Khan citizenship: Which country does the Delhi Belly actor belong to as he is asked to leave India by October 28?
In a subsequent post, Dipke argued that umpires should apply the rules impartially rather than make allowances for a player's personal achievement. He maintained that the pursuit of a century should not influence an official's decision during a match. His comments focused on a crucial moment in India's run chase. Kohli was closing in on his hundred, and India were also nearing the target set by Bangladesh.
 What happened in the India-Bangladesh World Cup match?
India were chasing 257 runs against Bangladesh in the league-stage match played in Pune. The Indian team had established control of the contest, with Kohli approaching another ODI century. The incident that prompted Dipke's reaction occurred in the 42nd over, bowled by Nasum Ahmed. A delivery down the leg side was not called wide by umpire Richard Kettleborough.
The decision drew attention because Kohli needed 19 more runs to reach his century, while India also required 19 runs to win. The two milestones were within reach at the same time. Kohli eventually completed his hundred with a six off Nasum Ahmed. He remained unbeaten on 103 as India defeated Bangladesh by seven wickets.
It was Kohli's 48th ODI century, bringing him closer to Sachin Tendulkar's record of 49 hundreds in the format. Kohli equalled the record during the 2023 World Cup semi-final against New Zealand and surpassed it in the final against South Africa.
 Why are Abhijeet Dipke's old posts being discussed now?
Dipke has recently been in the news over his protests at Delhi's Jantar Mantar and his demand for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. His protest attempts have also drawn the attention of the Delhi Police. His associates, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, have also featured in reports concerning the CJP's activities.
Amid these developments, Dipke's earlier social media posts have resurfaced. Critics have been sharing his past comments, including his criticism of the umpiring decision during Kohli's century. The cricket controversy and Dipke's current political activities concern different issues. However, the old posts have added another dimension to the online discussion surrounding the CJP founder .

docs.title: 2027 NFL Mock Draft Shocker: Arch Manning slides as Jeremiah Smith emerges as new No. 1 overall pick
docs.text:
The 2026 college football and NFL seasons are still underway, but that has not stopped analysts from looking ahead to the 2027 NFL Draft. While it’s too early to determine which NFL team will secure the first overall pick or which college prospect will emerge as the top choice, early mock drafts offer a glimpse into how the draft board could shape up next April. Arch Manning has been touted as the top QB prospect ever since he signed for the Texas Longhorns . However, despite completing his first full college season last year with a 10-3 record, he failed to lead Texas to the College Football Playoff.
 Texas is 4-1 with Manning as their shotcaller, but their recent loss to the Oklahoma Sooners in the Red River Rivalry has raised fresh questions about his draft stock. Manning struggled to impress in the high-profile matchup, throwing two interceptions and finishing with a poor completion percentage.
As a result, he is no longer widely viewed as the favourite to be the first overall pick or the top quarterback in the 2027 draft. Several mock drafts project him to fall outside the top spot, although he remains firmly in the conversation for a top-five selection. 
 JEREMIAH SMITH EMERGES AS A FAVORITE FOR THE 1ST OVERALL PICK
 Live Events
 You Might Also Like: 
 Bills vs Rams: Why was Aaron Donald's first sack since NFL comeback erased by a penalty? Watch viral video
While Manning's stock has taken a hit, Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith has emerged as a leading contender for the first overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. After three seasons at Ohio State, he could finally declare for the draft.
 Smith has continued to make his case with consistently impressive performances. He surpassed the 1,000-receiving-yard mark in each of his first 2 seasons and is well on course to do so in the 2026 season. He already has 916 yards in just 48 catches, averaging 19.1 yards per reception to go with 11 TDs.
In just 35 games for the Buckeyes, he holds the school record in receptions, receiving yards, and touchdowns. Widely regarded as one of the best wide receivers in college football, Smith has also emerged as a potential Heisman Trophy contender. His production, athletic ability, and big-play potential make him a compelling candidate to go first overall. No receiver has gone 1 st overall in 31 years.
 MOCK DRAFTS REMAIN DIVIDED ON 2ND OVERALL PICK
The race for the number 2 spot in the draft remains far less settled. Some mock drafts project Notre Dame cornerback Leonard Moore to go second overall, while others favour Oklahoma State quarterback Drew Mestemaker as the first quarterback selected in the draft. Both prospects have made compelling cases for a place near the top of the board.
 You Might Also Like: 
 Alaric Jackson punches Bradley Chubb after Bills' thrilling overtime victory; Video goes viral - What penalty could the Rams OL face?
Standing at 6’2, Moore was a consensus All-American last season as a sophomore, recording 31 tackles and 5 interceptions. PFF sees him as the 2nd overall pick while ESPN sees him going 4th. Drew Mestemaker's draft stock has been on the rise since moving to Oklahoma State from North Texas. His recent performances have been impressive, which could see him go up on the draft board. He could very well become the first QB taken in the 2027 draft.
Standing at 6’3, 215 pounds, he is blessed with great arm strength and the ability to deliver the ball downfield. Also, he is not shy to make plays with his legs.
So far this season, he has thrown for 1575 yards in five matches, with 13 TD passes and 5 picks. He could go 2 nd or 3 rd in the draft depending upon which team gets the spot and if they are in need of a QB.
 You Might Also Like: 
 WATCH: Aaron Donald gets into heated scuffle with O'Cyrus Torrence during Bills vs Rams MNF clash
 EDGE RUSHERS AND OFFENSIVE TACKLE ROUND OUT TOP 4
The fourth overall pick is another position where mock drafts remain divided. Some analysts favour an edge rusher, with Colin Simmons and Dylan Stewart among the names being considered. Others believe an offensive tackle could be the preferred choice, with Jordan Seaton and Trevor Goosby emerging as potential candidates.
Simmons is a 6’3, 245-pound prospect who is in his 3rd season of college football and leads the CFB in sacks with 9.5 so far in just five games, while Stewart stands at 6’5, 245 pounds and has registered 1 sack so far. But has great intangibles, which include his great length and movement.
Seaton, an offensive tackle for LSU, stands at 6’5, 311 pounds. He allowed only seven pressures in the 2025 season while lining up for 328 snaps. He possesses the ability to move in front of rushers and provides stable pass protection. His run game still needs a lot of work.
Longhorns LT Goosby is a 6’7, 325-pound prospect who played 492 snaps in 2025 and allowed 16 pressures and 3 sacks. He offers both pass protection and run-blocking and is capable of providing a full workload.
It will all come down to which team lands the fourth overall pick, and their choice will depend upon their roster needs. A team with an established QB could opt for an offensive tackle for better pass protection. However, a team that needs to strengthen its pass rush would go for an edge rusher like Simmons and Stewart.
 ARCH MANNING COULD STILL LAND IN THE TOP FIVE DESPITE HIS DRAFT SLIDE
Despite losing ground in the race for the first overall pick, Manning remains a potential top-five selection. His recent performances may have been concerning, but he still has talent, and long-term potential could still appeal to a team looking for a franchise quarterback.
However, he isn’t the only QB who could stake a claim at the 5th overall spot. Teams are also looking at Oregon's Dante Moore or Notre Dame's CJ Carr, and they could very well get drafted before the Longhorns signal-caller.
With several prospects capable of making a strong case for a top-five selection, the order remains fluid as the college football season

docs.title: She quit teaching at 51 after classroom burnout: 8 years later, Ella Love earns $100,000 cuddling stranger
docs.text:
Ella Love , 51, left her teaching job in New York to build a career around something most people associate with friends, family or romantic relationships: a hug. She now works as a professional cuddler and can earn up to $100,000 a year, according to a report by the New York Post.
 Her decision came after teaching became increasingly stressful. Limited classroom resources, recurring problems with students and little time for herself pushed her to look for a different kind of work. She wasn't initially planning to make cuddling her full-time career.
 She quit teaching at 51 after classroom burnout: 8 years later, Ella Love earns $100,000 cuddling strangers, and the reason clients keep coming back is unexpected ( Image source: Facebook)
“I was looking for something with a completely different energy, something that would calm me and center me. I didn't think this would become my profession,” Love told the newspaper. She started with an online course and continued teaching for another six months before deciding to focus on cuddling.
 Stress pushed her out of the classroom
Ella Love, 51, left her teaching career in New York because of stress, and she says she barely had any time for herself. Resources for education were scarce, and problems in the classroom were common.
 Live Events
 She told the New York Post she wanted something with a completely different energy, something calming. She never expected it to become her profession, and her words suggest she was after relief more than a business.
 She signed up for an online course and combined it with teaching for six months. Then she left the classroom to focus on hugs alone, and she’s now eight years in.
Most sessions last one to two hours, depending on the client. One ran as long as nine, which makes it the clear exception. Love says the work is simply an embrace, with no sexual component and no emotional attachment.
She screens clients beforehand to avoid unpleasant surprises. Not everyone is accepted, she says, because there’s a code of conduct and very clear boundaries. Screening lets her decline people before any contact begins, which matters when strangers spend hours in close contact.
Clients sometimes become aroused, and Love tells them that’s common before asking them to change position and relax so the hug can continue.
 Who books her, and what it earns
Her clients are usually people who have trouble with physical interaction, and some are on the autism spectrum. Love provides them with a safe environment.
Reports say she can earn as much as $100,000 a year. That’s a maximum, not a salary, and the coverage doesn’t say what she charges or how many clients she sees. For scale only: $100,000 across 1,000 one-hour sessions would be $100 an hour before costs. That’s an illustration, not her reported rate.
Her case isn’t exceptional. Platforms already exist that are dedicated to connecting people with professional cuddlers, which suggests enough demand to support dedicated businesses, though the reports give no numbers.

As preparations for the Union Budget 2026–27 gather pace, the groundwork underway signals a clear policy intent to accelerate domestic demand, revive private investment and generate employment, according to a budget note by Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL). The brokerage has identified five stocks across auto, agriculture, defence, financials and infrastructure themes, which it believes could deliver strong gains for investors.
 "The Budget is expected to focus on income-tax, GST, and customs simplification to enhance ease of doing business and support fiscal consolidation, alongside targeted support for agriculture, MSMEs, manufacturing, infrastructure, higher defence capex, EVs, and renewables through credit and incentives," the note authored by Research Analysts Sneha Poddar and Rekha Jaat said.
A strong capital expenditure thrust across highways, logistics, defence, rail freight corridors and connectivity is anticipated, complemented by emphasis on skilling, rural prosperity, women empowerment, AI adoption, climate action and digital finance to anchor India’s next phase of economic expansion, the note added.
The finance ministry started work on the Union Budget for 2026-27 from October 9 as per a circular issued by the Department of Economic Affairs (DEA).
The preparations come against the backdrop of an additional 50% US tariff on most Indian goods and other external headwinds. These have raised risks to India's growth and jobs outlook, prompting calls for stronger support to the export sector.
 Live Events
 5 stocks to buy: 
The stocks recommended by MOFSL are TVS Motor Company, UPL , Bharat Dynamics (BDL), M&M Financial Services and Dalmia Bharat , and each of these stocks has been assigned a 20% weight.
 1) TVS Motors: TVS Motors continues to outperform peers and is well-positioned to benefit from the budget’s push to boost domestic consumption and rural demand through higher allocations, income support, and infrastructure spending.
MOFSL said that improving rural sentiment, strong entry-level recovery and sustained two-wheeler demand will be key triggers. Moreover, the company's market share gains, easing discounts, and margin expansion will provide strong earnings visibility. The Apache and Ntorq maker remains its top pick in OEMs.
 2) UPL: The diversified agrochemical leader is well positioned to benefit from the union budget push riding on rural prosperity via higher agri credit, MSME support, and value-chain strengthening, lifting farmer incomes and crop-protection demand.
The company's strong points are stronger volumes, export tailwinds, improved working-capital discipline and post-bond-repayment balance-sheet strength, the brokerage note said. The company's rising focus on speciality chemicals supports solid 2HFY26 growth.
 3) Bharat Dynamics: Bharat Dynamics (BDL), a defence play, has a robust Rs 50,000 crore order pipeline over five years, with Rs 20,000 crore targeted in 2-3 years. This aligns with the expected defence capex surge and infra push.
The recent Rs 2.5 lakh crore DAC approvals for missiles, undersea warfare, and naval arms leverage BDL's tactical/strategic expertise, propelling FY31 turnover to Rs 100bn via indigenisation and lower provisions, the note said.
 4) M&M Financial Services: M&M Financial is poised for Union Budget 2026-27 benefits via rural prosperity, MSME credit, and employment focus, driving PV/tractor loan growth amid surging volumes from festive demand, GST cuts, and restocking.
The company targets Rs 3 lakh crore in assets under management (AUM) by 2030, which is at an 18-20% CAGR, bolstered by AI underwriting, lower credit costs, controlled opex, and margin stability for strong earnings visibility in retail portfolios.
 5) Dalmia Bharat: The cement company benefits from the budget’s infra capex surge, PMAY rural housing, and urban projects, driving cement volume growth.
Dalmia Bharat is a low-cost cement producer with high blending ratios, green power and low freight. The company is targeting 62 mtpa capacity by FY28, and its cost optimisation endeavours will likely lift EBITDA margins amid sector consolidation.

The markets worldwide are waiting with bated breath on what will be a historic policy announcement from the US Federal Reserve , where the central bank is expected to usher in a rate cut cycle.
 The announcement will be made at 11:30 pm IST (Indian Standard Time) on Wednesday.
If analysts are to be believed, the US Fed is all but certain to cut interest rates for the first time in more than four years.
However, there is no consensus on the quantum of reduction. Some are predicting a smaller cut of a quarter of a percentage point, while others believe a bigger half-point reduction is in the works.
Senior officials at the US central bank, including Powell, have indicated that a rate cut is coming, as inflation eases toward the bank's long-term target of 2%, and the labour market continues to cool in the post-Covid economy.
 Live Events
If the Fed starts the rate cut cycle, the Reserve Bank of India is also expected to follow suit.
A smaller cut would be a more predictable move, while a bigger cut would do more to boost demand — while also running the risk of reigniting inflation.
 WATCH LIVE TODAY: Press conference with #FOMC Chair Powell at 2:30 p.m. ET: https://t.co/1uJrua5qsH https://t.co/FJa6TbkDMt pic.twitter.com/87g5NJITsz 
— Federal Reserve (@federalreserve) September 18, 2024 
By the end 2024, markets are expecting a total reduction of at least 100 basis points in the first rate cut cycle in over 4 years since 2020.
But whether the Fed goes for 25 or 50 bps, the biggest trigger for stock prices to move up or down would be Powell's motivation behind the cut.
Asset classes from stocks, currencies and fixed income could all log swings in the immediate aftermath of the Fed decision.
While easing US interest rates are directionally positive for equities in general, “we should keep in mind interest rates are just one variable in a complex adaptive system that determines the direction of Indian equity markets”, said Anoop Vijaykumar, Investments and Head of Research at Capitalmind.

docs.text: Prabhudas Lilladhers research report on Waaree EnergiesWe recently visited Waaree Energies’ (WAAREEN) battery energy storage system (BESS) and inverter (including EMS facility) manufacturing plants in Rola and Sarodhi, Gujarat. The BESS assembly capacity of 5.15GWh was commissioned in Jul’26. Setting up 4GWh of cell capacity is underway, with planned operation by Dec’26. BESS offers WAAREEN an opportunity to broaden its renewable-energy manufacturing portfolio beyond solar modules and associated equipment. The extent of value addition will depend on the level of cell localization, system integration capabilities, execution and ability to secure profitable orders. The proposed 4GWh cell capacity could improve supply-chain integration if commissioned and operated successfully. WAAREEN’s inverter manufacturing capacity stands stated at 4GW, with utilization at ~58%. The company is targeting production of 5,000 inverters by Dec’26. The management indicated that the domestic C&I and retail inverter market is growing at 15-20% annually, and has potential to double over the next 2–3 years. WAAREEN is targeting a meaningful share of this opportunity while maintaining its pricing discipline. Waaree Power Pvt Ltd (under which inverter is manufactured) is expecting PCBA orders across multiple sectors,s including consumer electronics, automotive, technology, medical and defense.OutlookIncorporating BESS numbers in our estimates for FY28E/FY29E, we project revenue/EBITDA/PAT to log 22.5%/16.4%/8.9% CAGR over FY26-29E. We maintain ‘BUY’ with TP of INR3,115 valuing at 10x EV/EBITDA (Sep’28), implying PE of 18x Sep’28E.For all recommendations report, click hereDisclaimer: The views and investment tips expressed by investment experts/broking houses/rating agencies on moneycontrol.com are their own, and not that of the website or its management. Paytm shares have significantly outperformed the broader Indian stock market so far in 2026, but brokerage firm Nomura believes the fintech company has considerably more room to grow. Initiating coverage on One 97 Communications, the parent company of Paytm, Nomura has assigned a 'Buy' rating with a target price of Rs 2,250 per share, implying an upside potential of 31.4 percent from Wednesday's closing price.
The brokerage expects strong growth in Paytm's core payments and merchant lending businesses, supported by a leaner cost structure and operating efficiencies driven by artificial intelligence (AI). Nomura also sees additional growth opportunities from the proposed introduction of merchant discount rates (MDR) on select UPI transactions and international expansion.
 Paytm shares were trading 0.7 percent lower at around Rs 1,700 in Thursday's morning session, giving the company a market capitalisation of approximately Rs 1.09 lakh crore. Despite Thursday's decline, the stock has gained 31.6 percent so far in 2026, sharply outperforming the Nifty 50, which has fallen 12.4 percent over the same period.
 Share Markets Live Updates | Sensex, Nifty, GIFT Nifty Today 
Nomura expects Paytm's earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 96 percent between FY26 and FY29, reflecting its expectations of substantial operating leverage as the business scales.
The brokerage believes Paytm's core payments and merchant lending operations will remain the principal drivers of revenue growth. At the same time, increasing use of AI, economies of scale and disciplined marketing expenditure are expected to support a leaner cost structure.
Nomura has valued Paytm at 26 times its estimated FY29 enterprise value-to-EBITDA (EV/EBITDA) multiple, underpinning its target price of Rs 2,250. However, the brokerage flagged deterioration in lending asset quality and intensifying competition as key risks to its outlook.
Nomura's bullish assessment comes amid developments surrounding the introduction of merchant discount rates on select UPI transactions, which could create an additional revenue opportunity for payment service providers.
Earlier this week, the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) deferred the implementation of the proposed UPI MDR framework until after Diwali, triggering a sharp initial selloff in fintech stocks, including Paytm, Pine Labs and One Mobikwik Systems. The stocks subsequently recovered part of their losses.
Under the framework announced in September, a 0.4 percent MDR will apply to person-to-merchant UPI transactions exceeding Rs 2,000, with charges capped at Rs 300 for transactions of Rs 75,000 or more. Merchants, rather than consumers, will bear the charges.
Certain essential services, including railways, telecom, fuel and insurance, will attract a flat Rs 5 charge on transactions above Rs 2,000, while capital markets transactions will be subject to a lower MDR of 0.02 percent. The implementation date is yet to be notified.
NPCI chief Dilip Asbe had earlier indicated that approximately 96 percent of UPI transaction volumes and 75 percent of transaction value would remain outside the proposed charging framework.

OPINION | The rupee's problem is in the forward market, not the trade balance
docs.text:
- 
 The rupee recently slipped to about 96.70 against the dollar, close to its all-time low. This came just weeks after the RBI raised about $143 billion through the FCNR(B) and ECB route in three months. A cushion that large should have calmed the currency. It didn't, and that tells us the pressure doesn't come from where we usually look. 
 The trade and balance of payments (BoP) numbers don't explain it. India's BoP deficit was only about $5 billion in FY25 and US$24 billion in FY26. Yet, the RBI sold about $118 billion in FY25 (including forward liabilities) and $72 billion in FY26 to defend the rupee.
 If the underlying deficit is small but the dollar shortfall the central bank has to fill is several times larger, the extra demand is coming from somewhere else. That somewhere is the hedging market. 
 From a bigger import bill to a hedging rush 
 Two things have changed at once. First, the import bill has roughly doubled. Between 2017 and 2020, India's average monthly import bill for goods and services was about $50 billion. Today it is over $100 billion, roughly in line with nominal GDP growth.
 Second, importers are hedging far more of that bill. Put the two together and forward dollar demand has risen several times over in just a few years. That gap explains why the effective dollar shortfall has been close to $100 billion a year even as the reported BoP deficit stayed modest.
 How forward demand becomes spot weakness 
 The mechanism matters because this is where hedging turns into depreciation. When an importer buys dollars forward, the bank that sells the contract becomes short dollars for a future date. It covers that position by buying dollars in the spot market today, directly or through a buy-sell swap. So, every dollar hedged forward eventually becomes a dollar bought in spot. 
 Heavy hedging also pushes up the forward premium. Since June, it has risen by about 120 basis points, from 2.80% to about 4%. Once the premium rises above what the interest-rate gap between India and the US can justify, it creates an arbitrage.
 Selling rupees, holding dollars, and locking in the forward rate pays more than many rupee assets do. Capital moves out, the spot rate weakens, and rupee liquidity tightens. The higher premium also keeps foreign money out by increasing hedging costs for portfolio flows as well as regular ECB flows. 
 Even as exporter selling should theoretically pick up, expectations channel on further weakness on INR ensures that exporters, continue to hold back. With a forward premium of about 3.5% and expected depreciation of 3.5% -4% and above, selling dollars forward makes little sense to them. Importers bring their dollar buying forward while exporters delay their selling, and this lopsided behaviour is what widens the gap. 
 The result is a self-fulfilling loop. 
 Expected depreciation drives more hedging, more hedging pushes up premiums and spot demand, and a weaker rupee confirms the expectation. Under those conditions, the line between protecting a business and betting on the currency starts to blur.
 What the RBI is doing about it 
 The RBI's measures of 10 and 12 October go directly at this channel. 
 Cancelled hedges can no longer be rebooked. The limit for hedging without proof of underlying exposure falls from $100 million to $5 million. Banks must confirm that the same exposure hasn't been hedged with another bank.
 A new Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve (FERR) requires banks to keep 20% of the notional value of importer hedges above $2 million with the RBI in cash, earning no interest. The 12 October circular closed the remaining gaps. It extended the reserve to banks' own hedges and limited offshore non-deliverable contracts offered through GIFT City to genuine hedgers. Separately, a special window now supplies the full daily dollar needs of IOC, HPCL and BPCL, estimated at $8–12 billion a month, directly from the RBI and outside the interbank market.
 Will it work? 
 The optimistic case is that FERR discourages importers from rolling over hedges and higher forward premia encourages exporter selling. About $10 billion of hedges mature each month. If outstanding hedges fall by about $30 billion over two to three months, that creates a similar amount of net dollar supply. The rupee could then move towards Rs94 to a dollar by December.
 The more cautious case is that the reserve adds only about 10–12 paise a month to a three-month importer hedge. That is a small price for certainty when the spot rate has just dropped a full rupee. If oil stays high, importers may simply pay it. With continued pressure on the oil import bill and weaker capital flows and higher global rates, the depreciation pressure remains. In that case, the rupee would settle closer to Rs 96–96.5, and the RBI would keep having to step in.
 The measures also have side effects. Unremunerated FERR deposits, the higher daily CRR requirement and continued currency leakage together could cut durable liquidity. That would help an RBI now focused on fighting inflation, but it raises the risk of liquidity becoming too tight.
 Expectations are the real target 
 The October measures make betting against the rupee more expensive and buy the RBI time. They don't remove what drives the expectation of depreciation: a high import bill, muted FII flows as global equity money chases AI, and a shrinking gap between Indian and US interest rates. 
 Similarly, the channel of policy rate transmission works through the liquidity channel. Tolerance of surplus liquidity beyond what is required and thereby suppressing domestic money market rates creates enough opportunities for continued speculative bets on the currency. Addressing that possibly is the first step to ensure orderly near-term dynamics on the forex market. Some of the recent measures such as FERR, higher CRR daily maintenance and OMC window should indirectly achieve the same, which could possibly have been done more directly through a CRR hike, MSS issuances

docs.text: Shares of UltraTech Cement, Ambuja Cements, Shree Cement and other cement companies rose up to 3 percent in trade on Wednesday after strong June quarter results from peer Nuvoco Vistas Corp boosted sentiment across the sector.Nuvoco Vistas shares jumped as much as 17 percent to an over eight-month high of Rs 398 on the NSE after the company reported a strong performance for the June quarter, prompting brokerages to raise their earnings estimates.The stock has gained about 25 percent over the last two trading sessions following the announcement of its quarterly results.The companys better-than-expected earnings and positive management commentary strengthened expectations of an improvement in demand, pricing and profitability across the cement industry, leading investors to buy other cement stocks as well.UltraTech Cement rose 3 percent, while Shree Cement gained 2.5 percent and Ambuja Cements advanced 1.4 percent.The rally was broad-based, with JK Cement rising 1.4 percent, ACC gaining 1.8 percent and JSW Cement climbing nearly 2 percent.Following the results, brokerages turned positive on Nuvoco Vistas. During the post-results conference call, the companys management said it expects cement volumes to grow 7-8 percent during the remainder of FY27.HSBC said after the results that it expects better demand, pricing and cost conditions for the cement sector in the second half of FY27, despite seasonally weaker demand in the September quarter.The brokerage maintained its Buy rating on Nuvoco Vistas and raised its target price to Rs 475 after the company reported a stronger-than-expected June quarter, driven by higher realisations."We have had a strong start to the year, delivering higher business performance despite macro headwinds, particularly emanating from geopolitical tensions. The company achieved strong year-on-year growth in both EBITDA and PAT," Nuvoco Vistas Managing Director Jayakumar Krishnaswamy said.On the outlook, Krishnaswamy said the company will continue to focus on prudent procurement, cost optimisation and improving supply chain efficiency while remaining watchful of evolving geopolitical developments.Disclaimer: The views and investment tips expressed by investment experts on Moneycontrol.com are their own and not those of the website or its management. docs.title: Stock recommendations for 16 October from MarketSmith India
docs.text:
Markets 
 Stock recommendations for 16 October from MarketSmith India
 MarketSmith India 11 min read 16 Oct 2026, 06:15 AM IST 
 Summary
 MarketSmith India reveals its top stock recommendations for today, 16 October. Get expert insights into the best-performing stocks to guide your investment decisions. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 Stock market recap : On 15 October, Indian equities closed firmly higher with Nifty gaining 1.66% to 22,997, led by a strong rally in IT stocks. TCS, Infosys, HCL Tech, and Tech Mahindra have gained up to 12% more than three sessions as investors rotated money out of costly overseas AI stocks.
 Brent crude easing to about $104 and the rupee firming to 94.92 also lifted sentiment. Heavyweights Reliance, Bharti Airtel, and ICICI Bank, optimism about Q2 earnings, and short covering on Sensex expiry day added to the gains.
 However, hot US inflation revived bets on a Fed rate hike, Asian markets were weak, and foreign investors kept selling. PSU Banks and metals came under pressure, while Nestle, Canara Bank, and Yes Bank fell on stock-specific news, capping further upside.
 Two stock recommendations by MarketSmith India:
 Buy: Billionbrains Garage Ventures Limited (current price: ₹ 198) 
 Why it’s recommended: Strong growth in retail investing and financialization of savings, with Groww being one of India’s largest digital investment platforms and benefiting from increasing active investor penetration across the country. Expanding cross-selling opportunities across broking, MTF, wealth management, mutual funds, and insurance, supported by high customer engagement and technology-led scale. 
 Key metrics: P/E: 44.85, 52-week high: ₹ 227.20, volume: ₹ 1,103.03 crore 
 Technical analysis: Trendline Breakout 
 Risk factors: Revenue remains highly linked to capital market activity and trading volumes, making earnings vulnerable to market corrections and weaker investor participation. Regulatory changes by SEBI/exchanges on derivatives, broking, margin funding, or investor protection norms can impact transaction volumes and profitability. 
 Buy: ₹ 196–199 
 Target price: ₹ 228 in two to three days 
 Stop loss: ₹ 185 
 Buy: Krishana Phoschem Limited (current price: ₹ 212)
 Why it’s recommended: Capacity expansion in NPK/DAP fertilizers and ramp-up of the Meghnagar facility are expected to drive volume growth and improve revenue over the next few years. Strong backward integration in rock phosphate beneficiation, sulphuric acid, and phosphoric acid provides cost advantages and supports margin expansion. 
 Key metrics: P/E: 32.46, 52-week high: ₹ 213.99, volume: ₹ 38.46 crore 
 Technical analysis: Cup-base breakout 
 Risk factors: Dependence on imported raw materials and global phosphate/sulphur prices can create margin volatility and working-capital pressure. Fertilizer business is sensitive to government subsidy policies, payment delays, and regulatory changes, which can affect cash flows and profitability. 
 Buy at: ₹ 210–213 
 Target price: ₹ 245 in two to three months 
 Stop loss: ₹ 199 
 How Nifty 50 performed 
 Dalal Street turned firmly bullish on Thursday. Nifty 50 opened with a gap-up, holding above the previous close all session, and finished close to its high. The index opened at 22,671.30, touched a high of 23,056.40, a low of 22,637.40, and closed at 22,997.35, up 374.65 points (+1.66%). Breadth was strong, with 41 stocks advancing and only 8 declining. Tech Mahindra (+4.75%), ICICI Bank (+3.80%), and Reliance (+3.44%) led the gains. Nestle India (-7.76%) fell sharply despite strong Q2 numbers, followed by Adani Enterprises (-0.83%) and Trent (-0.72%). A decisive close above the 21-SMA supports a possible double bottom near 22,150.
 Momentum indicators are now turning in the bulls' favour. The MACD line (-262.22) has moved above its signal line (-317.78), and the histogram has turned positive at 55.56. However, both lines are still well below zero, so this is an early recovery rather than a confirmed uptrend. The 14-period RSI jumped to 49.94, sharply above its average of 33.37, and is now testing 50. A sustained RSI reading above 50 would confirm that buyers are in control. The steep slope of both indicators suggests short covering may extend in the near term.
 On the downside, 22,865 (21-day SMA) is the first support, followed by today's low of 22,640. 22,150 is the key base. On the upside, 23,050–23,100 is the immediate hurdle. Beyond that, the 50-SMA (23,580) and the 100-SMA (23,760) are the next targets, while the 200-SMA near 24,200 marks the long-term trend barrier. Macro cues offer some support: Brent eased to about $104, and the rupee firmed to 94.92. Against that, hot U.S. inflation has revived bets on a Fed rate hike, and the RBI's tightening stance remains a headwind. A close above 23,100 could extend the rally toward 23,500. Otherwise, the index is likely to consolidate between 22,650 and 23,100.
 How did Nifty Bank perform yesterday? 
 Nifty Bank opened on a positive note and briefly slipped below the previous close testing intraday lows. Buying at lower levels then fueled a sharp rebound. The index opened at 55,445.75, touched a high of 56,065.50, a low of 55,279.00, and closed at 55,810.50, up 494.50 points (+0.89%). BHEL reported a more than two-fold increase in consolidated net profit to ₹ 820.94 crore for the July-September quarter of FY27, compared with ₹ 374.89 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. The improvement was supported by higher revenue from its power and industry businesses. The company's total income rose 24% year-on-year to ₹ 9,553.01 crore in Q2, from ₹ 7,686.11 crore in the same period of the previous financial year. Revenue from the power segment increased to ₹ 6,637.90 crore from ₹ 5,675.64 crore a year ago. The industry business also recorded growth, with revenue rising to ₹ 2,662.45 crore from ₹ 1,836.16 crore in the year-ago quarter. However, BHEL's expenses climbed to ₹ 8,482.40 crore in the September quarter, compared with ₹ 7,201.54 crore in the corresponding period last year. BHEL is India's largest engineering and manufacturing enterprise in the energy and infrastructure sector, with operations spanning power generation equipment and industrial systems. Nuvama Institutional Equities retained its ‘Buy’ rating on Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd (BHEL) and raised its target price to ₹ 540 from ₹ 530, citing strong execution, improving margins and earnings growth prospects. The brokerage expects execution-led EBITDA margin expansion to 13.8% by FY29 and projects a 53% compound annual growth rate (CAGR) in earnings per share (EPS) over FY26–FY29. Nuvama said BHEL reported a strong Q2FY27 performance, with revenue rising 24% year-on-year and EBITDA margin expanding 330 basis points to 11%, well above the consensus estimate of 8.5%. Gross margin increased 590 basis points to 36.5%, reflecting the ramp-up of newer orders secured at better prices. However, fresh order inflows declined 85% year-on-year, taking the order book to ₹ 2.6 lakh crore, equivalent to 7.6 times FY26 sales. Nuvama cut its FY27 EPS estimate by 12% following management’s commissioning guidance. Its revised target price values BHEL at 38 times estimated FY28 EPS. JM Financial also maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on BHEL and raised its target price to ₹ 535 from an earlier level, valuing the stock at 30 times estimated September 2028 EPS. The brokerage cited improving execution, higher gross margins, a promising thermal power project pipeline and the company’s net cash position of ₹ 4,600 crore. JM Financial said BHEL’s Q2FY27 revenue rose 24% year-on-year to ₹ 9,300 crore, while gross margin improved to around 37%. EBITDA margin expanded to 11%, and net profit increased 119% year-on-year to ₹ 800 crore. Revenue from the power and industry segments grew 17% and 45%, respectively. The brokerage also highlighted improved working capital, with the cycle declining to 141 days from 164 days in FY26, supported by stronger collections and lower interest expenses. JM Financial raised its FY28 and FY29 EBITDA margin estimates to 13.2% and 15%, respectively, from 12.2% and 14.3% earlier, citing the improvement in execution and gross margins. docs.text:
Mint Money 
 New FEMA rules for foreign payments: what freelancers need to know
 Shipra Singh 6 min read 15 Oct 2026, 04:19 PM IST 
 Summary
 The reporting mechanism could help authorities identify suspicious transactions, including instances where services are falsely declared to move money across borders. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 Freelancers, consultants and small businesses receiving payments from overseas clients have to follow a new reporting compliance procedure under the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) foreign exchange rules. These rules, effective 1 October, apply to all professionals exporting services, such as content writers, digital marketers, designers, and any freelancers taking on gigs on global freelance marketplaces like Fiverr, Upwork, etc. 
 The Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2026 require service exporters to submit an export declaration form (EDF) to their authorised dealer bank. The form records details of services exported and payments due from overseas clients. 
 Earlier, such declarations largely applied to goods and software exports; they now also apply to services. The objective is to track export transactions and ensure that foreign exchange earnings are brought into India. 
 Vijaykumar Puri, partner at VPRP & Co LLP, chartered accountants, said the reporting mechanism could also help authorities identify suspicious transactions, including instances where services are falsely declared to move money across borders. 
 How and when is EDF filed? 
 Under the regulations, service exporters can submit one consolidated EDF covering invoices raised during a calendar month, within 30 days after that month ends. For example, invoices raised in October can be reported together by 30 November. 
 For services other than software, the regulations also permit EDF submission on or before the date payment is received, said Harshal Bhuta, partner at P.R. Bhuta & Co., Chartered Accountants. “Filing before receiving payment can make reconciliation easier. Otherwise, the bank may initially treat the receipt as an advance until it is matched with the relevant invoice later.” 
 The form should be submitted through the authorized dealer bank. Exporters can obtain the prescribed format from the regulations or ask their bank for its submission procedure.
 Chartered accountants (CAs) said that since the requirement started just this month, most of the banks are currently accepting physical forms to be submitted in bank branches. "We expect banks to move to a digital process soon. For instance, Axis Bank has just today integrated EDP reporting in their digital platform," said Bhuta. 
 For cross-border payments intermediaries such as Paypal, Wise, Skydo, etc, the declaration goes to the bank where the exporter's final rupee settlement is credited. "For all non-individual service exporters who are registered as businesses, the EDF needs to be submitted to the bank where final settlement happens," said Rohan Sewani, head - operations & customer experience, Skydo. 
 Why this declaration matters 
 While the declaration is a mandatory reporting requirement, it can’t obstruct international payments if it hasn't been filed, according to experts. “Banks have not been given additional powers to withhold payments merely because of an EDF mismatch,” said Puri. 
 However, you should not skip filing it as banks will reconcile the invoices reported in the EDF with the payments received from overseas clients. This includes checking the invoice amount, nature of services provided and purpose of the payment. Sewani said mismatches between invoice descriptions, Services Accounting Codes (SAC) – a unique six-digit code used under the Goods and Services Tax ( GST ) framework to classify GST rate for a service–and RBI purpose codes, or differences between invoiced and received amounts, could create problems during reconciliation.
 Bhuta said it is important that service professionals ensure that payments are correctly matched with invoices in RBI's Export Data Processing and Monitoring System (EDPMS). “Otherwise, an invoice could continue to show as outstanding even after the payment has been received. While delayed filing can be regularised, resolving old unmatched entries can become difficult”. 
 Exemptions and uncertainty 
 Bhuta said the regulations do not explicitly exempt any particular categories of service exporters. However, at a press conference on 7 October, RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra said individuals undertaking transactions of a personal nature, including tutoring and small software assignments for overseas clients, would be exempt from reporting.
 Experts said this has only added to the confusion, as whether this exemption covers all freelancers working independently remains unclear. “We are waiting for a FAQ (frequently asked questions) from the RBI that can clarify what the governor meant by ‘individual payments’,” said Bhuta. 
 Puri said small freelancers with incomes below a certain threshold should be exempted from this extra compliance. “Much of the information asked in EDF is already available. Exporters registered under GST already report their export invoices in their returns. Banks also collect information, including RBI purpose codes, when overseas payments are received. So what is the need for this new thing that replicates information?" he said. “An exemption threshold, similar to the ₹ 20 lakh GST registration threshold applicable to many service providers, would reduce the compliance burden on smaller freelancers.” 
 Meanwhile, till further clarity emerges, freelancers should check the applicable requirements with their banks and maintain proper records of invoices and international payments.

docs.title: NCERT brings personal finance to Class 9, but can one chapter build money habits?
docs.text:
Mint Money 
 NCERT brings personal finance to Class 9, but can one chapter build money habits?
 Ananya Grover 7 min read 15 Oct 2026, 11:50 AM IST 
 Summary
 NCERT’s new Class 9 chapter covers budgeting, saving, investing, insurance and tax. But teachers and experts say lasting money habits will depend on classroom practice, parental involvement and progressive learning. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 Budgeting, saving, investing, insurance, borrowing and income tax are now part of a single Class 9 chapter in CBSE-affiliated schools. The National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT) introduced it in its new Social Science textbook, Understanding Society: India and Beyond – Part 2, released on 28 September.
 Titled Managing Your Personal Finances , the chapter introduces personal finance through five pillars: income, budgeting, saving, investing, and protection and risk management.
 It begins with familiar situations, such as deciding whether to spend pocket money and festival gifts or save them in a gullak . Everyday examples explain inflation, purchasing power and compounding, including how someone who starts saving ten years earlier can accumulate substantially more than someone who starts later. Students also learn about fixed deposits, bonds, shares and mutual funds, insurance, the true cost of equated monthly instalments ( EMIs ) and income-tax calculations.
 But can one chapter translate this knowledge into lasting money habits?
 What already exists?
 Financial literacy in Indian schools has traditionally been fragmented, with many concepts taught through commerce, economics and accountancy at higher levels rather than through compulsory mainstream lessons for all students.
 NCERT has introduced economic concepts in earlier classes, too. In 2024, its Class 6 Social Science textbook included a theme called Economic Life Around Us , covering needs and wants, work, occupations, markets and exchange. Class 7 extended this theme with chapters on Banks and Magic of Finance , introducing money, banking, savings, borrowing and digital payments, including UPI.
 The Class 9 chapter builds on this foundation by focusing on personal financial decisions, from comparing investments and understanding risk to evaluating borrowing costs and calculating income tax.
 In the foreword, NCERT director Dinesh Prasad Saklani says the textbook aligns with the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 and the National Curriculum Framework for School Education (NCF-SE) 2023, which emphasise reasoning, responsible citizenship and preparedness for a changing world.
 Its inclusion in mainstream Social Science of Class 9 means students who later pursue science or humanities will also encounter financial concepts.
 Beyond terminology
 V. Pradeep Kumar, visiting professor and career and management consultant, said education should prepare students for everyday challenges, not just examinations. Introducing financial literacy in Class 9 can encourage responsible attitudes towards spending, saving and investment.
 However, exposure to concepts does not automatically translate into practical skills.
 Kunal Bhakat, a certified NISM and NCFE financial literacy trainer, said the chapter includes useful activities, such as preparing a budget for a new school year. But teachers need sufficient time to explain concepts, conduct exercises and discuss mistakes.
 “Without adequate time and continuity, students may learn the terminology without understanding how to apply it in everyday situations,” he said.
 If the chapter is treated primarily as an examination topic, students may learn to define compounding or income-tax slabs without knowing how to use these concepts in real life.
 What ICSE schools do differently
 The Council for the Indian School Certificate Examinations (CISCE) has published a teacher handbook, Financial Literacy: Integrating Financial Education in school curriculum. It states that financial education should not be treated as a standalone subject, but integrated into the curriculum for Classes VI-X in relevant contexts and in an age-appropriate manner.
 For example, in English and other languages, teachers can use suitable articles, stories and reports to introduce selected financial literacy concepts.
 The handbook also suggests activities such as role-play, games, case studies, surveys and discussions with experts. Some schools may choose to incorporate a supplementary textbook.
 “However, the actual impact of any book or curriculum ultimately depends on how effectively it is implemented in the classroom and how many opportunities students receive for hands-on learning,” Bhakat said.
 Parents' role
 From a behavioural standpoint, Anand Damani, a behavioural scientist and global speaker, believes teaching money should not be limited to classrooms. Schools should go deeper and gamify learning through the use of tokens. He also highlighted parents’ role in exposing children to money as soon as they begin to develop an understanding of the world around them.
 While children need not know their family’s net worth at a very young age, parents should begin by teaching them to see money as an enabler of their dreams and hobbies rather than associating it with status and power, he said.
 Financial education becomes more meaningful when children connect classroom lessons to everyday decisions, said Neha Singh, founder of Womoneysta and a certified financial planner whose daughter is in Class 9. The chapter provides a starting point and a structure for discussions around money, she said, but children also need opportunities to see how financial decisions work in practice.
 Shopping, she said, can become an exercise in budgeting. Asking a child to choose a birthday gift within a fixed amount introduces the idea of making choices within financial limits.

docs.title: 5 money lessons from international bestseller 'The Automatic Millionaire' by David Bach
docs.text:
A large salary is not the only starting point for building wealth, says David Bach. His international bestseller, The Automatic Millionaire, focuses on making saving and investing automatic. The book argues that regular systems work better than depending on discipline alone.
Published in the early 2000s, it encourages readers to put their financial future first. According to Bach, it is still one of the bestsellers on Amazon.
Here are 5 lessons from its approach, with some points for Indian readers.
Bach suggests setting aside a portion of every salary for savings and investments before spending anything. Most people pay bills, shop and save only what remains. Often, there is little left.
Automatic transfers reverse this habit by making saving the first payment after payday. Once the money moves away, it becomes harder to spend casually. The aim is to make saving a routine, without another monthly decision.
David Bach calls this idea the Latte Factor. A daily coffee, frequent snacks or an unused subscription may appear inexpensive. Over several years, these recurring expenses can add up to a sizable amount.
He recommends tracking spending for a few days to identify where money goes. This exercise can reveal costs that go unnoticed in busy routines.
The lesson is not to remove every small pleasure. Instead, find spending you can reduce and invest the amount saved. Cutting expenses alone does not create the same opportunity for long-term growth.
Detailed budgets can start with enthusiasm and disappear within weeks. Bach suggests creating arrangements that continue to work even when motivation wanes.
These systems direct money towards savings, investments and debt repayment before spending begins. Think of how an automatic EMI leaves your account each month. Savings can follow a similar pattern.
The approach reduces the need to repeatedly choose between spending now and saving later. Once arranged, it needs fewer monthly decisions.
Bach highlights retirement accounts offering tax benefits, including American 401(k) plans and IRAs. He recommends starting early and contributing regularly through salary deductions.
Compounding means your money can earn returns that, in turn, generate returns. Time helps this process work. Smaller amounts invested early can build substantial savings over many years.
Indian readers may consider EPF, PPF, NPS or mutual fund SIPs as local examples. These examples are not recommendations taken from Bach’s book. American account rules also do not apply directly in India.
An emergency fund helps protect savings when unexpected expenses or job losses occur. Without this cushion, people may borrow at high rates or sell investments at difficult times.
Bach also includes homeownership in his system, treating loan repayments as forced saving. However, buying a home should depend on affordability and personal circumstances.
He considers charitable giving another part of a rich life. Money can support others while also meeting personal goals.
His approach may require changes for people earning irregular incomes. Freelancers could save a fixed percentage of each payment. The central lesson remains consistent: create habits that make saving easier to continue.
