docs.text: If you are looking to invest in sectoral mutual funds, it is important to check market sentiment and the factors driving it.According to the latest quarterly note, Quarter of Divergence: Resilient India, Restless World, by Prateek Nigudkar, Senior Fund Manager at Shriram AMC, the first half of FY27 has seen a sharp divergence between large-caps and the broader market. The Nifty 50 gave up most of its first-quarter gains, falling about 6% in September alone.The Nifty 50 rose just 1.3% in H1FY27, while the Nifty Smallcap 250 gained 24.6%. Nigudkar attributes much of this performance gap to contrasting investment flows, noting that large-caps now offer better valuations relative to their historical averages.For mutual fund investors, however, sectoral opportunities need to be assessed against the relevant sector benchmarks, valuations, and underlying business prospects.Which sectoral mutual funds offer opportunities for mutual fund investors?Here is what investors can look at, along with benchmarks they can use to compare sector-focused schemes.Financial services: PositiveNigudkar is positive on banks and the life insurance segment, citing attractive valuations following the market correction. Several high-quality private banks are trading near or below their long-term average valuation multiples despite steady credit growth, stable asset quality and a strong economy.On life insurance, he flags regulatory uncertainty around the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India's (IRDAI) proposed rules on expenses of management (EoM) and distribution. However, Nigudkar expects the final regulations to be more measured, with longer implementation timelines and product-level flexibility.This means investors can compare relevant schemes with the Nifty Bank and Nifty Financial Services indices, while recognising that these benchmarks have different sector compositions.Automobiles: PositiveNigudkar remains positive on automobiles, citing attractive valuations and a recovery in volumes following GST-related changes. The festival season is a key near-term test of demand.He also flags raw-material inflation, particularly in steel, aluminium and precious metals, as a factor that could weigh on margins if manufacturers are unable to pass on higher costs.The Nifty Auto index can help investors assess the performance of automobile-focused funds against the broader sector.Power: PositiveNigudkar remains positive on the power value chain, supported by industrial activity, electrification, data centres and transmission capital expenditure.The Nifty Power index is a relevant benchmark for power-focused funds, while the Nifty Energy index offers broader energy-sector exposure.Healthcare: PositiveNigudkar is positive on healthcare and has added to hospital exposure following a sharp correction in hospital stocks.For comparison, the Nifty Healthcare index offers a broader healthcare benchmark, whereas the Nifty Pharma index is better suited to pharmaceutical-focused schemes.Transportation: PositiveNigudkar remains positive on the transportation sector, particularly ports and airports. He sees opportunities in ports, supported by government investment in port infrastructure.Real estate: Selective addNigudkar has added a developer from the National Capital Region (NCR), citing its large, low-cost land bank and strong pipeline of luxury housing launches. He sees resilience in premium housing demand and believes the land bank provides multi-year visibility on pre-sales.The Nifty Realty index can help investors compare the performance of real estate-focused funds with the listed real estate sector.Telecom: Neutral to positiveNigudkar's outlook is neutral to positive, as headline tariff hikes may be delayed until FY28.“ARPU should continue to grind higher through plan re-engineering and premiumization, and capex intensity is falling, but the near-term catalyst has moved out,” he added.

docs.title: Credit card reward points expiring? Why you should avoid unnecessary spending
docs.text:
However, when these points approach their expiry date, credit cardholders may feel pressured to redeem them before they lose their value. This raises an important question: Should you make a purchase simply to avoid losing your rewards? How should you handle expiring points, and what strategy should you follow?
The answer depends on the available redemption options, the value of the points, and an individual's budget. Spending more than planned to redeem expiring rewards can strain finances and potentially affect a person's credit profile if it leads to higher outstanding balances or missed payments. It can also defeat the very purpose of earning reward points.
Credit card issuers offer reward points, add-on services , promotional offers and other benefits to enhance the credit card experience. Cardholders should use these benefits to their advantage rather than feel compelled to redeem every point, regardless of whether doing so makes financial sense.
Before deciding what to do with expiring points, check your credit card issuer's terms and conditions. Review the validity period, redemption rules, available options and any restrictions. Depending on the card, points may be redeemable for merchandise, vouchers, bookings or statement credits.
Kaushik Chatterjee, founder and CEO of LendingPlate, explained, “Credit card reward points should encourage smarter spending, not unnecessary purchases. Consumers should evaluate the actual value of their points, available redemption options and expiry dates before making a decision. If redeeming points means spending more than planned, it may be better to let them expire than compromise their budget. The key is to use rewards strategically, without letting them dictate spending habits.”
Prudent credit card users should compare the value of different redemption options rather than assume that every point is worth the same. If a suitable redemption option is available without requiring additional spending, redeeming the points before they expire may make financial sense.
 The fear of losing accumulated points and rewards can encourage cardholders to buy products or services they neither need nor planned to purchase. Such spending can backfire, potentially outweighing the benefits of the rewards, particularly if it increases the outstanding balance on a credit card. 
Shakti Shekhawat, business head at BharatLoan, said, “Reward points can help consumers save money when used wisely, but chasing them can lead to unnecessary purchases. Consumers should check expiry dates, compare redemption options and understand any applicable restrictions. If using the points requires additional spending, they should consider whether the purchase fits their budget and serves a genuine need rather than making decisions out of fear of losing the rewards. ”
Ultimately, credit card rewards should complement planned spending, not drive it. Strategic planning is key. Redeem expiring points when you can do so sensibly, but do not stretch your budget or take on additional debt just to avoid losing them. Sometimes, letting a few points expire can be the more financially prudent choice.
 Disclaimer: This article is for general information only and should not be considered financial advice. Credit card users should review their card issuer’s terms and conditions and assess their individual financial circumstances before making redemption or spending decisions.

docs.title: How to make money using AI in the next 5 years: See freelancing, online courses, content creation and consulting options
docs.text:
AI offers several ways to earn through jobs, freelance services and online businesses. Over the next five years, you could explore options that match your skills. These include building websites, creating content, teaching online and helping businesses use AI. AI tools can draft text, generate code, analyse information and create images or audio. However, knowing how to use them effectively remains important. Start by understanding the work you want to offer and the skills it requires. Freelancers can use AI to prepare website designs and quickly generate a draft. They can also offer blog posts, website copy, product descriptions and marketing emails. Other options include writing ebooks, creating landing pages and offering translation services. AI can support these tasks and help manage administrative work. However, clients still need quality results. You need the skills to supervise output and deliver work that meets their requirements. Faster production may help you complete more assignments and increase earnings. But, when everyone is doing it, what helps you stand apart is the quality. AI can help create YouTube videos and social media marketing content. You could earn through advertising or use content to promote products through affiliate marketing. Another option involves turning AI artwork into physical products. Examples include printed artwork, mugs and T-shirts. This route differs from completing assignments for clients. Instead, you create content or products that can generate their own income. Your creative skills can help turn AI output into something people want. People with expertise in a subject can use AI to develop paid online courses. The tools can help organise lessons, prepare learning materials and create assessments. Existing documents, research papers, websites or videos can provide material for this process. AI can help arrange that information into a structured course. This option can suit people whose knowledge extends beyond writing or design. The technology can support content preparation while they contribute their subject expertise. Consulting offers another route for people who understand AI tools and business needs. You could help companies improve efficiency and introduce AI into everyday processes. For example, sales teams may need help using AI within customer relationship management systems. A consultant can teach staff ways to apply these tools. The work involves sharing knowledge and helping organisations meet their goals. It requires understanding how AI can support business activities. Longer-term options include becoming an AI engineer, a researcher, or a machine learning engineer. Other roles include data scientist, data engineer and AI product manager. These careers involve developing, improving or applying the technology itself. Training programmes can help you understand the skills required for such work. Start by exploring tools such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude. Learn how automation works and how to write clear instructions for AI. Creativity, empathy and adaptability also matter alongside technical knowledge. Practise using these tools for tasks connected to your chosen service or career. Then, decide whether freelancing, teaching, consulting or employment best matches your abilities. Disclaimer: This article is for general information and does not guarantee income or employment. Earnings depend on your skills, work quality, market demand and platform rules. Check AI-generated work for accuracy, originality and suitability before using or selling it. Also, you must clearly disclose AI-generated content to clients and audiences. Check and follow the relevant platform’s disclosure rules before publishing or selling such content. docs.title: Canara Bank shares crash 6% after Q2 results - Should investors buy, sell, or hold? Experts decode
docs.text:
Canara Bank shares crashed over 6% in morning trade on Thursday, 15 October, a day after the company reported its July-September quarter of the financial year 2026-27 (Q2FY27). Canara Bank share price opened at ₹124.65 against its previous close of ₹124.85 and dropped more than 6% to ₹116.80, almost close to its 52-week low of ₹116.55, which it hit on 1 October.
Canara Bank Q2 results 2026
During market hours on 14 October, Canara Bank reported an 8.40% year-on-year (YoY) rise in its profit for the September quarter at ₹5,175 crore. Net interest income (NII) for the quarter rose 20.39% YoY to ₹11,005 crore, while net interest margin (NIM) improved to 2.53% from 2.52% YoY.
Global deposits during the quarter saw a decent 13.13% YoY rise to ₹16,97,305 crore, and global advances also rose by a healthy rate of 19.46% to ₹13,75,060 crore.
On the asset quality front, gross NPA during the quarter declined by 102 bps to 1.33% and net NPA dropped by 24 bps to 0.30%.
The stock ended 3.87% higher at ₹124.85 on the BSE on 14 October.
However, in the next trading session, the stock declined due to heavy profit booking, with volume jumping more than 1.27 times.
Should investors buy, sell, or hold?
Experts appear largely positive about the stock after the bank's Q2 results.
Brokerage firm Motilal Oswal Financial Services has maintained a buy call on the stock with a target price of ₹160 and said it expects Canara Bank to deliver an FY27 RoA and RoE of 1.06% and 18.9%, respectively.
Motilal believes Canara Bank’s NIM may be range-bound at 2.5-2.6% for FY27, aided by rate hikes.
The brokerage firm underscored that Canara Bank maintains its loan growth guidance of 11-12%. The bank’s asset quality improved, with lower NPAs across asset classes. The bank will need to make additional provisions of ₹12,000-15,000 crore for the ECL transition, with an estimated impact of 1.0-1.2% on CRAR, said Motilal Oswal.
Brokerage firm Emkay Global Financial Services has maintained a buy call on Canara Bank stock with a target price of ₹150, saying it expects the bank to deliver 1% ROA over FY27-29E.
Emkay underscored that Canara Bank reported a largely in-line PAT and RoA, supported by higher NII, in-line opex, and lower-than-expected provisions, partly offset by lower other income.
It also delivered strong credit growth yet again, led by broad-based growth across segments as well as $3.2 billion FCNR B leverage, while maintaining a strong corporate pipeline of ₹50,000 crore, Emkay noted.
"NIM was stable, with management expecting it to sustain on the back of the recent rate hike. Asset quality continued to improve, while ECL provisioning requirement is estimated at ₹12,000- ₹15,000 crore (nearly 0.9-1.1% of loans), up by nearly ₹3000 crore amid elevated bond yields and potential MTM losses," Emkay observed.

 Festive hiring to rise 10-15% despite consumption woes, bonuses may shrink
 Vaeshnavi Kasthuril , Devina Sengupta 5 min read 15 Oct 2026, 06:00 AM IST 
 Summary
 Weak consumption, inflation, and pricier gadgets cloud hopes for sales. Flipkart and Amazon are expanding seasonal roles, but abundant labour and soft demand may keep bonuses largely flat. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 India’s biggest hiring season is here, but a consumption slowdown is clouding the outlook for festive recruitment in the organized sector.
 Yet seasonal hiring of contract and gig workers is expected to rise by 10-15% year-on-year, staffing agencies say, as e-commerce, consumer, logistics and auto companies pull out all the stops to drive sales amid a weak monsoon, inflation and tighter household budgets.
 Seasonal hiring by two of India’s largest e-commerce players offers evidence. Flipkart said it had increased festive-season job opportunities to more than 250,000, from over 220,000 in 2025. Rival Amazon India said it had created more than 160,000 seasonal job opportunities across its e-commerce and quick-commerce operations, up from over 150,000 in August 2025.
 However, performance-linked incentives for these additional workers may be muted, reflecting uncertainty over how strongly sales will pick up.
 “The drought will cause more agricultural workers to move to the metros, since the impact will be felt mostly in the rural belts. This will increase the availability of workers, and we see a 10-15% rise in demand this festive period compared to last year,” said Sunil Chemmankotil, country manager, human resources and workforce solutions company Adecco India.
 Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka have already declared drought conditions amid El Niño, a climate pattern marked by warmer-than-usual sea surface temperatures in the tropical Pacific Ocean.
 Typically, consumer -facing firms hire workers across metros, smaller cities and rural areas during the festive season. But water scarcity could push more workers towards cities in search of short-term jobs, keeping labour supply ample and limiting the need for higher payouts.
 “The bonuses and performance-linked payouts will remain similar to last year because companies will see a sufficient supply of workforce in the delivery, logistics, e-commerce, and retail sectors, which hire staffing during this period,” said Chemmankotil.
 Consumption blues
 Temporary workers are hired through third-party vendors and deployed at client sites for three to six months. Gig workers, typically in delivery services, may work for multiple companies. Both are in demand during India’s festive season, which begins around September and peaks in October-November around Diwali.
 Staffing firms begin hiring months in advance to help manufacturers, automakers and electronics companies prepare for the sales rush. Demand for gig workers , meanwhile, peaks during the festive period as delivery volumes rise.
 “Around Dussehra, if you find that customers are buoyant and demand has picked up, then that’s great. But we can’t tell now for sure,” said A. Balasubramanian, senior vice-president at staffing firm TeamLease.
 Similarly, workers move to urban areas and nearby towns for seasonal work during the festive period, then return to their farms towards the end of November. “Now there could be an additional spike, simply because work is even less now,” he said, referring to the possibility that farm distress could push more workers to seek jobs outside agriculture.
 Kartik Narayan, chief executive of online jobs marketplace Apna, noted that in smaller towns, where delivery volumes may be lower, workers may be less willing to take jobs without assured earnings, unlike in larger cities, where shipments are usually higher.
 The additional hiring comes amid mounting pressure on household budgets from rising inflation. Retail inflation accelerated to 5.54% in September, nearing the Reserve Bank of India’s 6% upper tolerance limit. The central bank raised its repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5% on 7 October, adding to pressure on household finances.
 Economists noted that 2025’s goods and services tax (GST) overhaul, which cut taxes on passenger vehicles, two-wheelers and premium consumer durables to 18% from 28%, unlocked pent-up demand across income groups, aided by easy credit availability. Discretionary spending among urban middle- and lower-income households has since held up in the first half of the current fiscal year despite rising inflation.
 But experts warn that the momentum may fade after the festive season , as a weaker monsoon threatens farm activity and rural demand, while car, electronics, and home prices keep rising, Mint reported on 29 September.
 Mint reported on 7 October that though input costs for most home and kitchen goods remain stable, they are rising for appliances, the segment’s largest by value. While major manufacturers are trying to hold back price hikes, companies have been raising prices across product portfolios. Smartphones, a key festive-season purchase, are also expected to see their steepest sales decline in a decade as memory chips become costlier, Mint reported on 17 September.
 TeamLease also pointed out that September was not a good month for several consumer-facing companies, including those selling consumables and appliances. Overall consumption could be weaker than expected, A. Balasubramanian cautioned.
 Flat wages 
 Recruiters said roles in picking, packing, shipping and delivery would pay ₹ 25,000- ₹ 50,000, including incentives, with compensation largely unchanged across most roles.

 Nestle better insulated from cost inflation than rural-heavy rivals: ICICI Sec's Manoj Menon
 Harsha Jethmalani , Pallavi Pengonda 6 min read 16 Oct 2026, 06:01 AM IST 
 Summary
 Menon also said that DMart should avoid copying quick-commerce models and instead double down on its price advantage to protect market share.

Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.

 FMCG and retail stocks are under pressure as inflation concerns and weak monsoons threaten India's consumption narrative. Nestle India shares plunged 8% on Thursday amid growing worries of cost inflation. 
 However, Manoj Menon, head of research and consumer analyst at ICICI Securities is of the view that diversified and premium-focused businesses such as Nestle could benefit from steady urban demand. In contrast, Dabur India and Emami are exposed to the risk of weak rural incomes. 
 Retail giant Avenue Supermarts ( DMart ) is also struggling with margin woes and intense competition from quick commerce (QC) companies. Rather than attempting to replicate 10-minute delivery models, Menon said that DMart's strongest defense is leveraging its price advantage where QC networks cannot compete profitably. Edited excerpts:
 DMart’s margin for the September quarter (Q2FY27) came as a disappointment, falling 30 bps (basis points) year-on-year to 7.3%, in the backdrop of cost pressures and stiff competition from QC companies. Avenue continues to scale store additions, but productivity remains subdued. It remains uncertain whether newer store ramps can offset this drag without diluting overall return ratios. What underlying factors are weighing on DMart's retail productivity?
 DMart’s retail productivity is under pressure. This is mainly due to competition from quick commerce and changes in DMart’s store network. Store-level analysis shows that about 80% of DMart’s trade areas already overlap with quick commerce services. These services are taking away frequent, small top-up purchases because they are more convenient. 
 At the same time, mature metro stores are reaching their physical capacity during peak hours. DMart’s rapid expansion—adding about 85 stores in FY26 to reach 500 stores—has also led to some cannibalization. New stores in tier-1 and tier-2 markets are growing faster than the company average, but they start with lower sales and take longer to reach full potential. In addition, high-margin general merchandise and apparel (GM&A) has stayed at about 23% of revenue, providing limited support to overall store sales. 
 Management has acknowledged that smaller-basket shoppers are migrating to QC due to convenience, a behavioral shift they expect to persist. You have also pointed out that the bigger risk for DMart is QC progressively increasing basket size and taking a greater share of planned household purchases. Given this, what changes can DMart bring to its existing offerings/model to defend its market share?
 Instead of changing its core business model to copy 10-minute delivery services, DMart’s strongest defence is to increase its price advantage in areas where quick-commerce companies cannot compete profitably. Management’s main priority is to keep prices lower for weekly and monthly grocery shopping, so value-conscious households have no financial reason to move planned purchases to convenience apps. 
 At the same time, DMart is expanding its store network in a disciplined way, with a target of adding about 15% more stores each year. This will bring stores closer to customers in underserved areas, reduce travel inconvenience, and use the lower property and operating costs in tier-1 and tier-2 markets to protect returns. 
 On the digital side, DMart Ready supports the main business instead of becoming a high-cost growth channel. It focuses on scheduled delivery of large orders within six hours in densely populated and profitable areas. DMart is also strengthening its non-food FMCG and GM&A ranges, where dark stores do not have enough shelf space or supply-chain scale to compete effectively.
 With inflation pinching household budgets hard and weaker monsoon, how are value-focused retailers having a wider presence in tier-2 and tier-3 markets expected to fare in H2FY27? Are margin compression risks intensifying? Which retailers would be more impacted?
 Value retailers in tier-2 and tier-3 markets will perform differently in H2FY27 depending on whether they mainly sell essential goods or discretionary clothing. High food inflation and weak cash flow in rural areas are forcing middle- and lower-income households to spend more on basic food. As a result, fewer customers are visiting stores for non-essential items, and people are buying clothes less often.
 The risk of lower margins could rise for value apparel retailers as store operating costs remain high. At the same time, raising prices in price-sensitive semi-urban markets can reduce sales volumes. This forces retailers to offer large discounts to clear unsold stock. Therefore, regional and semi-urban value fashion chains such as V-Mart Retail, Style Baazar, and City Kart are likely to face greater pressure on margins. 
 In comparison, large grocery discount retailers such as DMart and mixed-format retailers such as Vishal Mega Mart are likely to be more resilient because price-sensitive customers may shift to discount stores to reduce their household grocery spending. 
 El Nino conditions and rising raw-material costs are key risks to growth and margins of FMCG companies. Which FMCG companies are likely to be the worst hit from a near-term perspective? And which ones are likely to do well, and why?

docs.title: Reliance Power shares crash 5% as ED seizes ₹2,033 crore assets in FEMA case against Anil Ambani firm - What's next?
docs.text:
The seized assets include Reliance Power’s bank balances and its shareholding in Sasan Power Ltd, the ED said in a statement. The seizure order was issued on 12 October under Section 37A of FEMA. Responding to the action, Reliance Power said in a regulatory filing that it disputes the allegations and will take all appropriate steps, as advised by its legal counsel, to protect its interests and those of its shareholders and other stakeholders, PTI reported. According to PTI, the ED investigation stems from a Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) action regarding write-offs or provisions of ₹ 2,101.46 crore recorded in Reliance Power's books. These related to overseas investments and advances made to companies in the British Virgin Islands (BVI) and the Cayman Islands. The ED said the investigation traces back to 2006, when Reliance Natural Resources Ltd, which has since merged with Reliance Power, raised $300 million through foreign currency convertible bonds. Of this amount, $275 million was invested in its wholly owned Singapore subsidiary, Reliance Natural Resources (Singapore) Pte Ltd (RNRL-S). RNRL-S subsequently deposited the funds with Deutsche Bank (Suisse) SA in Geneva. The deposits were then used as collateral for loans extended to entities incorporated in the BVI, according to the ED, as reported by PTI. The agency alleged that these BVI entities were controlled and managed from India by the Reliance Anil Ambani Group through front persons acting on the group's directions. The ED's investigation found that the loan proceeds were used for various purposes, including the alleged temporary round-tripping of funds into India through foreign entities based in Mauritius. The agency claimed that the transactions benefited the group, while funds were parked overseas. According to the ED, the BVI entities failed to repay the loans extended by Deutsche Bank. The agency further alleged that documents were fabricated to show that RNRL-S and Reliance Power's Indonesian subsidiaries had provided advances to these entities for apparently legitimate business purposes. The ED alleged that the documents were backdated to portray the transactions as genuine business dealings, PTI reported. Reliance Power share price today opened at ₹ 19.68 apiece on the BSE, the stock touched an intraday high of ₹ 19.84 per share, and an intraday low of ₹ 18.80 per share. Rajesh Bhosale, Technical Analyst at My Advisor Alpha, said Reliance Power shares remain in a downtrend, with every bounce attracting selling pressure. He placed the next support at ₹ 17.50 and resistance at ₹ 20.50. Virat Jagad, Senior Technical Research Analyst at Bonanza, said Reliance Power remains in a sustained downtrend, falling 3.58% to ₹ 19.12 and trading below all its key moving averages, indicating continued selling pressure. The stock is forming lower highs and lower lows, reflecting a weak technical structure. Its RSI of 31.22 signals strong bearish momentum, with the stock nearing oversold territory. Jagad placed immediate support at ₹ 19, followed by ₹ 18.50, with resistance at ₹ 21.50. A sustained move above ₹ 21.50 would be needed to signal a potential recovery, whereas a break below ₹ 19 could trigger further downside.  The cat and mouse game continues to keep us guessing on where the trends are going to move thus making it very challenging for us to take the next step. However, in the current scenario we can note that the overall trends have not matured and is causing problem for a revival.
 On 14 October 2026, Indian equities reflected a mix of volatility and cautious optimism. The Nifty 50 closed at 22,622.70, down 99.25 points or 0.44%, after oscillating between 22,558.95 and 22,757.95 during the session. The Sensex also slipped modestly, mirroring profit-booking in select heavyweights.
 Three stocks to trade, recommended by NeoTrader’s Raja Venkatraman:
 ICICIGI ( Cmp 1713) 
 ICICIGI: Buy above ₹ 1720, stop ₹ 1650 target ₹ 1910 (Multiday) 
 Why it’s recommended: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Limited is the largest private sector general (non-life) insurance company in India. Since July 2026 the stock has been in a correction mode. As the market showed signs of revival and after correcting by nearly 10% the stock has reached some important support region around 1440. The revival seen from lower levels has been encouraging. A strong thrust always attract some buying interest and support from Relative Strength Index(RSI) could help the prices rebound. Go long. 
 Key metrics: 
 P/E Ratio : 35.31, 
 52-week high: ₹ 2064.15 
 Volume: 505.64K 
 Technical analysis: Support at ₹ 1620, resistance at ₹ 2100. 
 Risk factors: Concentration in motor segment, data security & privacy vulnerabilities and investment portfolio fluctuations. 
 Buy : above ₹ 1720. 
 Stop loss: ₹ 1650. 
 Target price: ₹ 1910 (2 Months) 
 BHEL (Cmp 464)
 BHEL: Buy above ₹ 466, stop ₹ 439 target ₹ 510 (Multiday) 
 Why it’s recommended: Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL) is India’s largest state-owned engineering and manufacturing enterprise in the energy and infrastructure sectors. There has been a long period of consolidation and ahead of the numbers some upward drift had already emerged. The strong breakout above consolidation supported by increasing volumes has created a new opportunity. With strong Q2 numbers to support and with the support from the bands strong demand could emerge to the head higher once again. With the Relative Strength Index (RSI) also not giving up we can expect the upward drive to continue. 
 Key metrics: P/E Ratio : 66.84, 
 52-week high: ₹ 455.90, 
 Volume: 37.46M. 
 Technical analysis: Support at ₹ 420, resistance at ₹ 550. 
 Risk factors: Long-Gestation Projects, Intense Market Competition and Regulatory and Evolving Compliance Pressures. 
 Buy : above ₹ 466 
 Stop loss: ₹ 439 
 Target price: ₹ 510 (2 Months) 
 FIRSTCRY (Cmp 181.65)
 FIRSTCRY: Buy above ₹ 183, stop ₹ 175 target ₹ 201 (Multiday) 
 Why it’s recommended: FirstCry (legally known as Brainbees Solutions Limited) is India's largest omnichannel retail platform for mothers, babies, and kids' products. There has been steady decline since last one year. However, as the markets are now showing some signs of revival the stock is also bottoming out making a double bottom. A small hint at a potential upmove that could unfold in the coming days. Look for initiating a buy. 
 Key metrics: P/E Ratio : 74.55, 
 52-week high: ₹ 369.65, 
 Volume: 1.92M. 
 Technical analysis: Support at ₹ 1020, resistance at ₹ 1300. 
 Risk factors: State-Controlled Pricing & Taxation and input cost pressure. 
 Buy : above ₹ 183 
 Stop loss: ₹ 175 
 Target price: ₹ 201 (2 Months) 
 Stock market recap 
 The broader chart shows Nifty struggling to sustain above 22,700, with momentum indicators like RSI hovering near 43, suggesting subdued strength and limited conviction among buyers.
 Recent sessions have highlighted sectoral divergence. IT stocks staged a strong rebound earlier in the week, driven by earnings optimism, while banking and realty indices provided support. However, metals, pharma, and PSU banks have remained under pressure, keeping benchmarks capped. Small-cap indices continue to outperform, signaling selective risk appetite despite headline weakness.
 Macro concerns persist, with crude oil prices elevated above USD 104 per barrel and retail inflation at 5.54 percent, raising caution over margins and policy flexibility. The rupee has extended its rebound, aided by RBI’s intervention, but global cues remain mixed.
 Outlook for trading 
 Hesitation continues to be one of the key dominating emotion that curbs the strong resolve to move higher. As the trends attempt to hold over the next few days the long body candle revival has once again assured that the trends are beginning to take shape as a steady buying participation was witnessed through the day! The rupee has begun to cool off as global markets are now getting settled with the volatility after the central bank tightened the screws on speculative bets against the currency, putting it on track for its best single-day gain in a while, when policymakers had also resorted to extraordinary measures to stabilise it.
 From a technical perspective, Nifty remains in a consolidation phase after recent volatility. The index closed at 22,622, slipping 0.44%, and continues to oscillate within a broad 22,450–22,900 band. Price action shows repeated attempts to reclaim 22,700, but selling pressure near resistance has capped upside momentum. The candlestick structure reflects indecision, with intraday recoveries failing to sustain into the close.

CAS review: Sebi announces last 30-minute VWAP method for settlement
 Sebi has revised the closing auction session framework, adopting the last 30-minute VWAP for derivatives settlement and changing trading hours from December 7, 2026.
 Sebi has revised the closing auction session framework, introducing changes to settlement pricing, trading timings and order transitions, with key provisions taking effect from December 7, 2026. (Photo: Reuters)
 Khushboo Tiwari Mumbai 4 min read Last Updated : Oct 16 2026 | 12:08 AM IST
 Listen to This Article
 The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) on Thursday announced the much-awaited revisions to the closing auction session (CAS) framework, introducing changes to the settlement methodology, trading timings, and the transition of unexecuted iceberg orders. 
 An iceberg order is a large order split into smaller orders where only a fraction of the total quantity is visible in the order book displayed to the public. The revised framework will take effect from December 7, 2026, except for changes relating to the transition of unexecuted limit and iceberg orders from the continuous trading session (CTS) to CAS, which will come into force from February 8, 2027. 
 Retaining the earlier method, the settlement price of index derivatives will be based on the volume-weighted average prices (VWAP) of constituent securities during the last 30 minutes of the CTS (3.00 pm to 3.30 pm) in the equity cash segment.
 For expiring stock derivatives, clearing corporations will determine settlement prices using the VWAP of the underlying stock during the last 30 minutes of the CTS across all stock exchanges. 
 Exchanges will provide the VWAP and quantity traded to clearing corporations and continuously disseminate indicative values to market participants in real time during this period.

 Under the revised timings, CAS will operate as a separate 10-minute session from 3:30 pm to 3:40 pm on all trading days. The order-entry period will close randomly between 3:38 pm and 3:40 pm. 
 Trading in index derivatives will continue until 3:45 pm on regular trading days, but contracts expiring that day will stop trading at 3:30 pm. Trading in stock derivatives will continue until 3:45 pm, including on expiry days. The post-close session in the cash segment will run from 3:50 pm to 4 pm, with trades executed at the closing prices of securities. 
 CAS became effective on August 3 and saw an uproar from the trading community over the settlement price, sharp spikes, and low liquidity. 
 The latest changes were announced following a consultation paper that received over 20,000 suggestions, which was followed by deliberations of the market regulator’s Secondary Market Advisory Committee on Thursday. 
 The regulator had also proposed a blended mechanism, on which several market participants had raised concerns, given the low liquidity in the window.
 Traders and brokers had favoured the 30-minute VWAP method stating that participants were more familiar with this mechanism and that it was more transparent and operationally well understood. 
 On Thursday, Sebi also specified how unexecuted orders will move from the CTS to CAS. Pending limit orders will generally be carried forward, except stop-loss orders and orders priced beyond the applicable CAS price bands. 
 Unexecuted iceberg orders within the applicable price bands will be converted into fully disclosed limit orders (at fixed/pre-determined price), unless market participants opt out when placing the original orders. These converted orders will have lower time priority than other limit orders carried forward from the continuous session, but higher priority than limit orders placed during CAS. 
 At present, CAS is a 20 minute window from 3:15 pm to 3:35 pm where the reference price calculation and transition from CTS to CAS happens from 3:15 pm to 3:20 pm. In this period, no order entry is allowed. The next five minutes order entry period remains. From 3.25 pm to 3.30 pm, the order entry period is restricted to limit orders only, and no modifications or cancellations of market orders are allowed. In this period, trading closes randomly in the last two minutes. 
 In its consultation paper, Sebi had also proposed prohibiting cancellation of limit orders placed beyond 1 per cent range of the reference price during CAS. However, the regulator skipped this change in the final circular. What’s new 
 Stock derivatives’ settlement prices will use underlying stocks’ volume-weighted average prices across exchanges
 CAS will run from 3:30 pm to 3:40 pm, with random closure
 Expiring index derivatives will stop trading at 3:30 pm; stock derivatives at 3:45 pm
 Iceberg orders will become fully disclosed limit orders unless participants opt out

IPO proceeds will make us net-debt-free company: Jio Platforms MD
 Industrialist Dhirubhai Ambani, the founder of the group, took Reliance Textile Industries, which later became RIL, public in 1977
 Akash Ambani, MD, Jio Platforms, speaks at a press conference in Mumbai on Thursday Photo: KAMLESH PEDNEKAR
 Pravin Palande Mumbai 4 min read Last Updated : Oct 15 2026 | 11:50 PM IST
 Listen to This Article
 The initial public offering (IPO) of Jio Platforms, the digital arm of Reliance Industries Ltd (RIL), is the first from the group in nearly two decades. Jio Financial Services Ltd listed in August 2023 following its demerger from Reliance Industries. There was no IPO.
 Industrialist Dhirubhai Ambani, the founder of the group, took Reliance Textile Industries, which later became RIL, public in 1977. What makes this IPO special is that, unlike the other big issues in the past, it has no offer for sale.
 “The full proceeds take us to be a net-debt-free company,” said Akash Ambani, managing director of Jio Platforms.
 The Reliance family has presented the issue as an offer that leaves money on the table for shareholders. At the top end of brand values, Jio is valued at 34 times its FY26 earnings per share, while Bharti Airtel, its closest listed rival, trades at about 39 times.
 “Part of Reliance’s philoso­phy, and one that really has been passed on to us from my grandfather’s time, is to create shareholder value,” Isha Amb­ani, RIL non-executive director, said at a press conference in Mumbai on Thursday. “It is most important to be able to price this attractively so that shareholders who come in can create long-term value along with the growth of Jio Platforms.”

 The IPO will begin on October 21, with a price band of Rs 1,065-1,119 a share. The company has 533 million customers and carries about 60 per cent of India’s wireless data traffic. In 2025-26 (FY26), it earned nearly Rs 1.47 trillion in revenue; Rs 76,255 crore in earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation; and Rs 30,049 crore in net profit.
 From Reliance Textile to Jio 
 Uday Kotak, founder of Kotak Mahindra Bank, linked the issue to Reliance’s first public offer when as a 15-year-old he had seen celebrations in Marine Drive. This inspired him to get into financial services. “The RIL group, since 1977, has believed in making it attractive for investors to be long-term with the group,” Kotak said.
 That offer had brought a generation of small investors into the market, and Reliance has built its identity around them since.
 Isha Ambani said RIL had delivered a 29 per cent annualised return since that listing. “For him (Dhirubhai Ambani), Reliance was never just a company. Reliance is a promise that every Indian should have the opportunity to participate in India’s growth, to share in India’s prosperity,” she said of her grandfather, who popularised the IPO culture in India. “Three generations later, we carry forward not only his vision but also the trust of millions of shareholders who believed in his vision and made it their own.”
 She said the group judged its businesses against two goals. “The first is that we like to create and protect fortress-like balance sheets, and the second is that we steer our businesses towards generating compounding free cash flow,” she said. “Financial prudence is embedded in our DNA.”
 She pointed to Mukesh Am­bani’s promise in 2019 to make RIL net debt-free by 2021. “Covid came along with it, and along with that came a global slowdown. And yet, nine months ahead of schedule, that promise was delivered on. And that is what shareholder commitment means to us at Reliance.”
 Uday Kotak said investors’ demand shaped the price of the issue. 
 The design of the issue 
 After the IPO, RIL’s stake will fall from 66.43 per cent to around 64.5 per cent. Meta’s affiliate Jaadhu Holdings holds 9.98 per cent and Google has 7.73 per cent.
 Within the issue, Rs 2,500 crore is reserved for RIL shareholders and Rs 500 crore for employees, who will get a 5 per cent discount. Half the net issue has been set aside for qualified institutional buyers, 35 per cent for retail investors, and 15 per cent for non-institutional investors. The anchor book, about 30 per cent of the issue, opens on October 19. The issue closes on October 23 and the shares are due to list on the BSE and the NSE on October 28. Nineteen book-running lead managers are handling the issue.

Higher mutual fund yields lift ICICI Prudential AMC's Q2FY27 earnings
 ICICI Prudential AMC posted 18% revenue growth in Q2FY27 on higher mutual fund yields, while net profit rose 6% and equity market share declined amid competition
 premium 
 ICICI Prudential AMC’s Q2FY27 operating revenue rose 18% year-on-year to ₹1,670 crore, while net profit increased 6% to ₹890 crore.
 Devangshu Datta 5 min read Last Updated : Oct 15 2026 | 11:00 PM IST
 Listen to This Article
 ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company (AMC) reported steady September quarter numbers.
 Operating revenue grew 18 per cent year-on-year (Y-o-Y) (7 per cent quarter-on-quarter or Q-o-Q) to ₹1,670 crore in Q2FY27.
 Yields came in at 57.9 basis points (bps) versus 56 bps in Q2FY26 and 56.1 bps in Q1FY27.
 Operating revenue mix stood at 89.9 per cent for mutual funds, 8.7 per cent for alternative investment funds (AIFs) and 1.4 per cent for advisory.
 Total operating expenditure at ₹460 crore was up 23 per cent Y-o-Y (up 6 per cent Q-o-Q).
 Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (Ebidta) came in at ₹1,230 crore, up 16 per cent Y-o-Y and 7 per cent Q-o-Q.
 Ebidta margin was at 72.6 per cent.
 Net profit stood at ₹890 crore, up 6 per cent Y-o-Y but down 8 per cent Q-o-Q. Net profit margins came in at 53.1 per cent versus 58.8 per cent in Q2FY26 and 61.7 per cent in Q1FY27.
 The board approved the acquisition of ICICI Securities’ portfolio management service (PMS) business, which is expected to expand the client base and complement existing offerings.
 The unique customer base grew 3 per cent Q-o-Q to 17.8 million as of September 2026. Total investment book stood at ₹5,190 crore. 
 Income beat expectations with higher revenue due to rising mutual fund yield at 48 bps.
 The market share in net equity flows declined through April-August to 11 per cent from 19 per cent in FY26 with a drop in small & midcap (SMID) as well as flexicap.
 Overall equity market share declined by 29 bps Q-o-Q to 13.8 per cent.
 PMS/AIF businesses had healthy growth. Equity quarterly average assets under management (QAAUM) (including balanced) was ₹6.62 trillion, up 4.4 per cent Q-o-Q.
 Revenue was up 3.4 per cent at ₹1,540 crore. Non-mutual fund revenue was 3.7 per cent lower.
 Core income was ₹1,180 crore. Other income was lower at ₹16.9 crore and the tax rate was 25.8 per cent.
 Core net profit was ₹876 crore. Core net profit yield was 28.3 bps.
 The share of equity (including balanced) was up by 40 bps Q-o-Q to 57.3 per cent, while debt declined 103 bps to 15.4 per cent and liquid rose by 40 bps to 6.9 per cent.
 The share of exchange-traded funds (ETF) was up 16 bps up to 13.1 per cent.
 The management said the rising MF yield is due to net equity flows shifting from bigger size schemes (low-yield) to lower-size ones (higher-yield).
 But equity market share declined owing to weak relative performance and low presence in SMID/flexicap. There's an industry-wide trend where smaller players are raising their equity share.
 Systematic investment plan (SIP) and systematic transfer plan (STP) flows declined from June 2026 by 4.1 per cent to ₹4,670 crore in September 2026, due to a shift towards SMID.
 The AMC is cautious on SMID and is waiting for better valuations.
 The PMS+AIF QAAUM was up 6.4 per cent Q-o-Q to ₹55,100 crore, and the acquisition of I-Sec’ PMS business is expected to expand its customer base.
 PMS QAAUM grew 21.4 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹30,790 crore. Advisory business QAAUM fell 6.5 per cent Q-o-Q to ₹25,900 crore due to foreign institutional investor (FII) outflows. The management is developing investment structures abroad to prepare for potential recovery in foreign inflows.
 Overall, industry QAAUM grew 5.1 per cent Q-o-Q (13.4 per cent Y-o-Y) to ₹87.5 trillion in Q2FY27 and equity-oriented AUM grew by 15.3 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹48.2 trillion.
 Industry net equity flows was ₹1.06 trillion in Q2FY27 (down 7 per cent Q-o-Q). Mid and smallcap funds continued to attract the highest inflows, with their combined share up to 36 per cent in H1FY27 from 22 per cent in FY26. SMID delivered far higher returns in H1FY27 compared to Nifty 50.
 The customer base increased 11.1 per cent Y-o-Y to 63 million. Passive QAAUM grew by 23 per cent Y-o-Y. For ICICI AMC, the specialised investment fund (SIF) QAAUM increased to ₹4,950 crore in Q2FY27 from ₹2,680 crore in Q1FY27.
 The AMC has launched four funds and plans to introduce a fifth fund during Q3FY27.
 The management remains optimistic about SIF with economics similar to MFs, with higher ticket-size and greater flexibility.
 The AMC launched a balanced hybrid fund, a multi-asset active fund of funds (FoF), a dynamic asset allocation passive FoF, and BSE insurance ETF and lifecycle funds with 5-, 10- and 15-year maturities.
 The management is conservative in its use of derivatives and treasury management. The AMC intends to scale its segments (listed equity, private credit, real estate, private equity and early-stage private equity) before entering infrastructure. It sees expansion of SMID as a 5-7 year opportunity.
 The results have not shifted the needle much in terms of analyst consensus though valuations remain at elevated levels.

docs.title: 3 ‘Buy’ recommendations by Jefferies with 20% to 25% upside
docs.text: Investors tracking stocks with potential upside after the September quarter earnings season may want to look at three companies covered by global investment bank Jefferies. Jefferies has maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on Groww, Leela Hotels and ICICI Lombard, with potential gains of 20% to 25% from the respective target prices. Its outlook rests on different factors, ranging from improving trading activity and hotel demand to insurance claims and regulatory changes. Let’s take a look at stocks Jefferies is bullish on and what is the rationale behind it - Jefferies on Groww: Buy, target price Rs 240; 25% upside Jefferies has retained its ‘Buy’ rating on Groww with a target price of Rs 240, indicating an upside potential of 25%. According to the report, the company’s September 2026 quarter profit after tax (PAT) was 5% above estimates, supported by higher cash equity revenue and lower operating expenses. Groww’s retail cash equity market share increased to 15.4% in the September quarter, compared with 15.1% in the June quarter. Its margin trading facility (MTF) book also grew 15% sequentially to Rs 4,400 crore. Jefferies noted that improved risk controls helped the company avoid significant one-off costs during the September market sell-off. ALSO READPorinju Veliyath’s latest moves: A Rs 256 cr cash play and a stock at half book value Another change is the declining contribution of options trading to revenue. Options accounted for 45% of revenue, down from 72% in FY24. While this reflects a shift towards revenue diversification, the number of options orders fell 14% quarter-on-quarter, partly due to the impact of the Closing Auction Session (CAS) framework. Jefferies expects the resolution of CAS-related concerns to support a recovery in options activity. It also sees potential in Groww’s recently launched United States stock trading service. According to the report, if US stock orders reach one-third of the volume generated by its commodities trading product, they could contribute around 9% of estimated PAT in financial year 2028. Jefferies on Leela Hotels: Buy, target price Rs 735; 24% upside Jefferies has raised its target price on Leela Hotels to Rs 735 from Rs 675 while maintaining its ‘Buy’ rating, implying an upside potential of 24%. As per the report, the hotel operator’s September quarter revenue rose 33% year-on-year, while earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) increased 36%. The performance was driven by a 30% rise in revenue per available room (RevPAR), primarily due to higher average room rates. Demand from domestic travel and meetings, incentives, conferences and exhibitions (MICE) also supported growth. Leela’s EBITDA margin expanded by around 120 basis points year-on-year to approximately 46%. Management has also raised its growth outlook, expecting EBITDA to increase at a high-teens rate in the second half of FY27. This implies mid-20s growth for the full year, according to Jefferies report. The global investment bank has increased its estimates for revenue per available room growth and raised its EBITDA and PAT estimates by 3% to 7%. However, the company’s expansion plans and the pace at which new properties contribute to earnings remain important factors to watch. Jefferies on ICICI Lombard: Buy, target price Rs 2,050; 20% upside Jefferies has maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on ICICI Lombard General Insurance with a target price of Rs 2,050, suggesting an upside potential of 20%. Jefferies' assessment follows an improvement in the insurer’s claims performance in the September quarter. According to the report, ICICI Lombard’s loss ratio stood at 72.7%, better than Jefferies’ estimate of 74%. The loss ratio measures the share of premiums used to pay claims, making it an important indicator of an insurer’s underwriting performance. ALSO READNomura initiates coverage on Paytm; sees 32% upside as India’s fintech mkt hits $109 bn Retail health insurance grew 64% year-on-year, while new business in two-wheeler motor insurance increased 51%. However, fire insurance premiums declined 21% due to competition. The combined ratio, which compares claims and operating expenses with premiums, came in at 107%, higher than the brokerage’s estimate. Jefferies believes proposed commission regulations could benefit ICICI Lombard by putting pressure on smaller insurers with higher commission costs. It also expects the company to benefit from its claims management record. The global investment bank has cut its FY27-28 profit estimates by around 4%, but retained its ‘Buy’ rating. docs.title: Nomura initiates coverage on Paytm; sees 32% upside as India’s fintech mkt hits $109 bn
docs.text: India’s fintech industry is one of the largest and most sophisticated ecosystems in the world. The domestic fintech market’s revenue is expected to more than double by 2031, and this growth will be led by the unified payments interface (UPI). Paytm, operating under One97 Communications, sits at the centre of this expansion story. Japanese brokerage Nomura has initiated coverage on Paytm with a ‘Buy’ rating and a target price of Rs 2,250. This implies an upside of nearly 32% from the stock’s current price of Rs 1,706. India's Fintech market revenue may reach $109 bn by 2031 The domestic fintech market is expected to reach $109 billion in revenue by 2031, from $51 billion in 2026, Nomura said, citing data from Mordor Intelligence India fintech market. Digital Payments are set to expand around three-fold, reaching around $10.2 trillion by FY30, the brokerage said, citing data from Indian payments handbook – 2025-2030. ALSO READ25%+ sales growth: 2 auto ancillary stocks eyeing more revenue from every vehicle “In this context, companies such as One 97 Communications (Paytm) with meaningful scale, entrenched and trusted consumer and merchant relationships, AI-led technology capabilities, robust compliance frameworks, and strategic partnerships with regulated financial institutions appear best positioned to capture the next phase of growth in India's digital financial services landscape,” Nomura said. Nomura on Paytm: Core biz to drive revenue growth The company’s core payments business functions as an infrastructure annuity on India's expanding digital payments rails. Nomura has projected the GMV of this business to expand at a 25% compounded annual growth rate (CAGR) over FY25 to FY29. It also expects rising credit penetration, such as credit cards, RuPay credit cards on UPI, credit lines on UPI, to lift net payment margin to 5.26bp, excluding MDR, by FY29 from 4.03bp in FY26. “This is complemented by Paytm's dominant position in the Merchant Lending business. Paytm's merchant lending penetration stands at just 8% of its 15.7 million base currently (subscription merchants), which we estimate has room to expand to 11% by FY29F – reflecting significant white space,” it said. Nomura on Paytm: AI as the biggest structural driver “For Paytm, indirect expense optimization remains a core margin driver, in our view. We expect a reduction in total indirect costs from ~50% of revenue in FY26 to 34.1% by FY29F, as revenue growth is likely to outpace cost growth. Employee costs should see the sharpest decline – from 30.7% in FY26 to ~19.8% of revenue – driven by AI-led efficiencies in field sales, merchant acquisition, and commercial negotiations,” the brokerage said. It expects technology costs to fall from 7.6% to 5.9% of revenue on economies of scale. Marketing costs, in contrast, could stay elevated near 3% of revenue through FY29, reflecting a brand reinvestment strategy. Nomura expects Paytm’s cost structure to improve across the board, with AI as the biggest structural driver. Nomura on Paytm: Merchant Discount Rate, the next leg of growth Nomura sees UPI MDR revenue, the launch of proprietary AI product “Pi” for banks and insurers, and selective international expansion, driving the company’s growth. ALSO READAther to M&M, Hyundai: Nomura names 5 stocks to ride the EV shift in India “.given Paytm's exposure to smaller merchants and exempted categories, we expect ~20% of its GMV to be MDR eligible at ~8bp,” it said, adding that this translates into incremental revenue of Rs 500 crore over FY28 and Rs 620 crore over FY29. “Paytm is pursuing selective international expansion, leveraging its India-tested payments technology and distribution playbook through asset-light, partner-operated licensing and select direct-operated entries, but we expect meaningful earnings contribution only from FY30F,” it added. Paytm: Growth across the board Paytm’s growth story is in focus and Nomura sees 32% upside. MDR, AI, and core business growth are expected to drive earnings hereon, along with selective international expansion. docs.title: How Rs 158 crore Nagastra deal gives boost to India’s private defence sector
docs.text: The Indian Army took delivery of 450 Nagastra 1R loitering munitions — significantly boosting its short-range precision-strike capabilities. The missiles were developed indigenously by Solar Defence and Aerospace Limited for kamikaze-style attacks against enemy targets. Loitering munitions have assumed an increasingly important role in modern warfare and even played a role during Operation Sindoor. According to the Department of Defence Production, loitering munitions are aerial weapons equipped with a built in warhead. It is also known as a suicide drone, kamikaze drone, or exploding drone — designed to ‘loiter’ in a specified area until a target is identified. “These munitions offer faster reaction times against concealed targets that appear briefly, without requiring high value assets to be near the target area. Additionally, they allow for more precise targeting, as the attack can be adjusted or aborted mid-flight,” the DDP website explains. Variants used by India: Nagastra Nagastra 1R Nagastra FPV Nagastra 1B Man Portable LMS Nagastra 2 Nagastra 2B Nagastra 3 According to defence officials, the Nagastra -1 can neutralize any hostile threat with GPS-enabled precision strike with an accuracy of 2m in its 'kamikaze’ mode. The man-portable fixed-wing electric UAV of weight 9 kg has an endurance of 30 min, a man-in-loop range of 15 km and an autonomous mode range of 30 km. Its electric propulsion system provides a low acoustic signature to make it undetectable by the enemy at a height of more than 200 metres. India’s first indigenous loitering munition One of the first major foreign procurement of loitering munitions came in 2009 as the Indian Air Force signed a $100 million deal with Israel Aerospace Industries AI Harop ‘suicide’ drones. The weapons were designed as a cross between drones and missiles — reportedly deployed during Operation Sindoor to neutralise Pakistani air defense systems. The Indian military has also expanded its arsenal over the past few years by placing orders for locally assembled and joint-venture systems. News agency ANI reported in June 2024 that the first indigenous loitering munition — known as Nagastra–1 — had been delivered to the Indian Army. The military had placed an order for Solar Industries' subsidy Economics Explosives Limited to supply 480 loiter munitions under Emergency Procurement Powers. According to a subsequent report by Financial Express, Solar Industries India had also announced in December 2024 that it had secured export orders worth Rs 2,039 crore for the supply of advanced defence products. These were set to be delivered by the company and its subsidy (Economic Explosives Limited or EEL) over the next four years. The announcement came mere weeks after Solar Industries said it had secured a Rs 399.4 crore export order that must be completed within three years. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh noted in January this year that Nagastra drones were used during Operation Sindoor. He revealed that the missiles manufactured by the Solar Group had accurately struck terrorist targets — thereby proving its strategic capability. Singh also noted that more advanced versions of Nagastra were now being developed. The May 2025 clash had also prompted the government to boost its military arsenal — using emergency procurement powers to order small loitering munitions and mini surveillance drones from domestic private sector companies. The two contracts were reportedly worth a collective Rs 295 crore. According to reports, the first deal was struck with Nagpur-based Solar Defence and Aerospace for 450 Nagastra-1R loitering munitions or kamikaze drones that are capable of night operations at a cost of Rs 158 crore. The second deal was reportedly worth Rs 137 crore and struck with ideaForge Technology for hybrid mini unmanned aerial vehicle systems that are variants of the Switch drones with vertical take-off and landing capabilities. Record Rs 1,577 crore contract The Defence Ministry also signed contracts with TATA Advanced Systems and NIBE earlier this year for procurement of loiter munition systems, weapons and other accessories. According to a PIB release shared on August 14, the Rs 1,577 crore deal will be procured under the Buy (Indian) category through Fast Track Procedure. “The Loiter Munition System is a critical equipment developed to enhance the capability of the artillery regiments — thereby strengthening the overall operational effectiveness of the Indian Army…The procurement marks a pivotal step towards modernising and empowering Indian defence industries,” the press note reiterated. It is believed to be the largest single one-time order for long-range loitering munitions in the country. The Defence Acquisition Council had also accorded an Acceptance of Necessity for various proposals in December 2025 — amounting to a total of about Rs 79,000 crore. The list included procurement of loiter munition systems for artillery regiments. Need for emergency procurement India had fast-tracked emergency financial limits after Operation Sindoor in 2025 — concluding procurement contracts worth Rs 1981.90 crore under the Emergency Procurement mechanism. Key equipment being procured included integrated drone detection and interdiction systems, low level lightweight radars, very short range air defence systems and loitering munitions, including Vertical Take-Off and Landing systems and various categories of drones. According to an analysis shared recently by the Impact and Policy Research Institute, assessments after Operation Sindoor highlighted military requirements “in areas including unmanned aerial systems, counter-UAS and loitering munitions. The report added that these gaps should not be attributed solely to procurement delays — also reflecting evolving operational requirements and emerging technology needs. “These shortcomings show that the acquisition system can struggle when technology develops faster than established procurement cycles. docs.title: For missile accessory contract, defence PSU picks only one firm, set up by its ex-CMD, wife
docs.text: By Pratyush Deep For the first time in three years, Bharat Dynamics Ltd (BDL) has turned to a private company to supply optical sights for its missiles and it has done so raising questions of conflict of interest and propriety. Citing ‘urgency’, the Hyderabad-based defence PSU issued a ‘single tender’ – without competition – for the optical sights to a company that its former Chairman and Managing Director Siddharth Mishra and his wife set up after he retired. Today, that company is 95 per cent owned by Mishra’s wife, Shambhavi Mishra. In May this year, BDL issued a ‘single tender’ to Aindri Defence Advisory Private Limited for the supply of 300 optical sights – within seven months – following the completion of acceptance and validation tests of five sample units supplied by the company. These five units are to be supplied within a month of BDL placing a purchase order. And Aindri Defence Advisory has cleared the technical evaluation stage, according to the Government e-Marketplace portal. It has quoted a price of Rs 56.8 crore for the tender. ALSO READBharat Dynamics Q1 profit jumps to Rs 118.79 crore, revenue more than doubles A financial evaluation of its bid is underway. What is a ‘single tender’? A “single tender” is a non-competitive route in which only one vendor is invited to bid. Norms allow it only when just one supplier can meet the requirement, or when the need is urgent. This tender also requires the supplier to provide technical support for at least 15 years for maintenance, repair and overhaul of the sights. What are optical sights? Optical sights are a critical part of the aiming and target-acquisition system of an anti-tank guided missile, or ATGM. The operator uses the sight to locate and track the target and to align the missile with it. They work by receiving infrared radiation from missiles, converting the input into electrical signals, and transmitting them to coordinator units on the ground. Explained: Optical sights in anti-tank missiles An optical sight in this context typically comprises lenses, an eyepiece, a sighting reticle, and a housing with protective components, mostly manufactured in India. Bharat Dynamics Ltd's portfolio includes Konkurs-M - a mechanised infantry ATGM manufactured under licence from a Russian company. In 2022, the PSU signed a Rs 3,131.82-crore contract with the Indian Army for the manufacture and supply of Konkurs-M, which can be fired from a specialised infantry combat vehicle or a ground launcher. Aindri Defence Advisory Company records show that Aindri Defence Advisory was incorporated in May 2024 by Siddharth Mishra and his wife, each of whom held 50 per cent. Mishra retired from BDL in March 2023 after four years as its CMD. He was a director and shareholder of the company from its incorporation until January 2025. He left when he was appointed Member (Technical) at the National Company Law Tribunal, Kolkata. Shambhavi now holds 95 per cent and is a Director. The other director, Kaushiki Nandan Vatsyayana, holds the remaining 5 per cent. Mishra and Shambhavi did not respond to text messages or calls from The Indian Express seeking comment. The company did not respond to questions emailed to the address provided in its filings with the Registrar of Companies. Vatsyayana said he could not share information about the BDL tender. The locked office of Aindri Defence Advisory Pvt Ltd at the National Small Industries Corporation (NSIC) campus in Kushaiguda, Hyderabad. (Photo credit: Nikhila Henry) BDL did not reply to queries from this newspaper. 2026 tender marks major commercial shift BDL bought the same type of optical sights in 2024 and 2025, but both purchases were competitive and limited to the public sector. The 2024 tender was open only to Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs). The 2025 tender was open to CPSEs and Defence Public Sector Undertakings. Data from the GeM portal shows India Optel Limited, a Mini Ratna PSU under the Ministry of Defence, won both. The 2026 tender drops both competition and the public-sector restriction. It is addressed only to Aindri Defence Advisory, making this the first time in the three years of these procurements that the order may go to a private firm. ALSO READRs 158-cr Nagastra order completed: Indian Army receives 450 indigenous Kamikaze drones BDL cites urgency as its reason for choosing this route. The tender states: “The competent authority in the Ministry or Department has certified that the demand is urgent, and any additional expenditure involved by not procuring through advertised tender enquiry is justified in view of urgency. The Ministry or Department has placed on record the nature of the urgency and reasons why the procurement could not be anticipated.” The reasons, however, are not spelled out. The shift also shows how the tenders treat Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs). The 2024 and 2025 tenders were formally exempted from the MSE purchase preference through approvals from the competent authority. The 2026 tender applies it. Under the preference, eligible MSEs and original equipment manufacturers quoting within 15 per cent of the lowest price (L1) can be offered the chance to match L1. If they do, they can win up to 25 per cent of the order quantity. An engineer, Mishra served in the Indian Navy for more than three decades until 2016. He then spent three years as a General Manager at Electronics Corporation of India Ltd before joining BDL as CMD in 2019.

docs.title: Rs 1.86 lakh cr grid push: 2 ‘under-the-radar’ transformer stocks with 40%+ ROCE
docs.text: India’s rising power demand is creating a need for higher investment in transmission infrastructure. Industrial growth, urbanisation, data centres and electric vehicles are increasing electricity consumption. Peak power demand has already touched 270.8 GW and is projected to reach 500 GW and beyond by 2036. To meet this demand, state utilities and private developers are investing in transmission lines, substations, and power evacuation infrastructure. Government programmes such as the Green Energy Corridor, with a ₹1.86 lakh crore outlay for intrastate transmission, are adding to the investment pipeline. India plans to invest around ₹9 lakh crore in power transmission by 2032. As the grid expands, demand for high-voltage transformers, which play a critical role in transmitting electricity, is expected to rise as well. The industry is currently dominated by large and established players such as Hitachi Energy India, CG Power, Siemens Energy India and Transformers and Rectifiers. These companies have diverse business capabilities across the power value chain, from transmission to High Voltage Direct Current. FE Stock Insights on WhatsApPGet instant alerts on high-conviction investment themes and fundamental deep dives—direct from Financial Express.Join now Alongside these established names, companies such as Atlanta Electricals and Voltamp Transformers bring a more concentrated presence in the transformer market. Likewise, this article covers two lesser-discussed small-cap transformer companies that are also positioning themselves to benefit from this investment cycle. #1 Kanohar Electricals: Moving Up the Voltage Ladder, Targeting Higher Margins Kanohar Electricals (market cap: 8,309 crore) manufactures equipment for power transmission utilities, Indian Railways, and renewable energy infrastructure. Its main product lines include power transformers up to 500 MVA and 400 kV, Scott-connected traction transformers for railways, and shunt reactors. The company operates two production units in Meerut, at Gangol and Rithani, with a combined annual capacity of 19,200 MVA. Capacity utilisation stood at 29.7% in FY25 and 46.0% in FY26, before reaching 36% in Q1FY27. Management expects the existing manufacturing capacity to support operations through FY28. Navigating Seasonal Lulls and Capacity Typically, transformer deliveries are lower in the first quarter, with the majority occurring in H2 and peaking in Q4. This is the reason for the low capacity utilisation in Q1FY27. Transformer manufacturing accounts for about 85% of revenue. Engineering, Procurement, and Construction (EPC) projects for substations and transmission lines make up around 15%. The company is focusing more on higher-margin, high-voltage transformers like 400 kV and 765 kV. Products in the 400 kV category accounted for roughly 70% of manufacturing revenue in Q1FY27. Management is also developing the capability to manufacture 765 kV transformers for future extra-high-voltage projects. The 765 kV Shift and a ₹20,000 Crore Railway Opportunity It will take 3 to 4 years to achieve commercial qualification for 765 kV tenders. Further, ongoing railway modernisations, high-speed rail lines and dedicated freight corridors require specialised Scott-connected traction transformers. Traction transformers are used in railway electrification to supply power to electric trains. Management estimates this market represents a potential opportunity of around ₹20,000 crore over the next 5 to 10 years. The company is adding 18,000 MVA of incremental capacity at the Gangol facility. This plant is designed to manufacture 765 kV extra-high-voltage transformers. The new capacity is scheduled to serve demand starting in FY29. For FY27, the management has set a target of ₹950 crore in consolidated revenue. The company expects the EBITDA margin to remain at the same level as in FY26. Growth will primarily be driven by higher manufacturing volumes and a product mix focused on the 400 kV segment. This order book has an execution timeline of 18-24 months, providing strong revenue visibility. Government entities account for 88.4% of the order book, while private sector clients make up 11.6%. This extends the working capital cycle to roughly 120 days. The company aims to maintain its revenue growth (45%) momentum into FY28. At 45% growth on the ₹950 crore expected revenue in FY27, revenue could reach approximately ₹1,350 crore to ₹1,400 crore. At a realisation rate of over ₹6.1 lakh per MVA, the projected volumes support the company’s targeted revenue of approximately ₹1,350-₹1,400 crore. In Q1FY27, the company's revenue from operations rose by 103.5% year-on-year to ₹137.1 crore. EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortisation) increased by 152.2% to ₹38.8 crore, while the margin expanded by 550 bps to 28.3%. Net profit grew by 140% to ₹27.3 crore. The margin expanded due to higher manufacturing volumes and a shift toward higher-margin 400 kV equipment. The historical track record is robust. Over the last three years ending FY26, revenue has grown at 28% CAGR while net profit has grown at 80% CAGR. #2 Indo Tech Transformers: Expanding Capacity to Capture Rising Transformer Demand Indo Tech Transformers (market cap: 3,437 crore) manufactures a broad array of transformer equipment serving power grid infrastructure and industrial sectors. Products include distribution transformers, power and large power transformers, special applications (inverter, converter) and renewable applications. Across its operating history, Indo-Tech has manufactured over 66,000 transformers. docs.title: India’s Rs 19,744 crore green hydrogen push has a fertiliser connection: 3 stocks to watch
docs.text: India's fertiliser industry is approaching a transition that could reshape how manufacturers source one of their most important raw materials. Pilot projects for green ammonia (produced with renewable electricity and green hydrogen) are being replaced by long-term supply contracts. The government, under the ₹19,744 crore National Green Hydrogen Mission (NGHM), has allocated 7.24 lakh tonnes per annum (TPA) of supply across 13 fertiliser units at discovered prices ranging from ₹49.75 to ₹64.74 per kg. The agreements aim to replace imported fossil-fuel-based ammonia, improve supply security and reduce emissions. The Ammonia Switch: Could Cleaner Fertiliser Inputs Mean Stronger Margins? Green ammonia could offer fertiliser manufacturers something more valuable than a lower carbon footprint: a different way to manage one of their largest input-cost risks. Conventional ammonia is made using hydrogen derived largely from natural gas, linking its production cost to global gas prices and exposing buyers to international supply disruptions. Green ammonia uses hydrogen produced through renewable electricity to reduce dependency on fossil fuels during production.
