If manufacturers can source contracted green ammonia at a competitive delivered price, they may gain better visibility on part of their future input costs. That could help them plan production and reduce exposure to sudden changes in conventional ammonia prices. Domestic green ammonia production could also cut dependence on imports over time. Moving ahead, the key question is which listed fertiliser companies have progressed furthest from policy participation to commercially meaningful adoption. We identified three such companies. #1 Paradeep Phosphates: The NPK Fertiliser Maker With a Defined Green-Ammonia Allocation Paradeep Phosphates Limited (PPL) manufactures phosphatic and nitrogen-phosphorus-potassium (NPK) fertilisers, including di-ammonium phosphate (DAP) and complex fertilisers. Its manufacturing network spans Paradeep in Odisha, Goa and Mangalore, with operations supported by phosphoric acid, sulphuric acid and ammonia-related infrastructure. This integrated footprint makes raw-material availability and pricing important to production costs. Green ammonia could eventually change the company's sourcing mix. Two Allocations, Two Confirmed Locations in the Company's Disclosures PPL's allocation under the Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) auction totals 100,000 TPA: 75,000 tonnes for Paradeep at ₹55.75 per kg and 25,000 tonnes for Zuarinagar, Goa, at ₹62.84 per kg. SECI identifies ACME Cleantech Solutions as the selected supplier for both locations. The allocation gives PPL a defined route towards adopting green ammonia at existing manufacturing facilities, but the two prices also show that the economics are not uniform across plants. The important distinction is between a supply allocation and a realised operating benefit. In its February 2026 investor call, management described the arrangement as being at a preliminary stage and indicated that supply could take another two to three years. The next meaningful milestones are a confirmed offtake agreement, the scheduled commencement of supply and evidence that the contracted volume is being delivered. Acid Capacity and Fertiliser Volumes Strengthen the Operating Context PPL's Q1FY27 investor presentation lists ammonia capacity of approximately 290,000 TPA at each of its Goa and Mangalore facilities. Its Paradeep operations include 500,000 TPA of phosphoric acid capacity and 2 million TPA of sulphuric acid capacity. The company reported that higher sulphuric acid production following capacity expansion supported its Q1FY27 performance, while the first phase of its phosphoric acid expansion from 500,000 to 700,000 TPA remained on track. These investments can strengthen raw-material integration, but they should not be confused with green-ammonia project expenditure. PPL does not separately report green-ammonia revenue, earnings or realised cost savings. Its ₹250 crore aluminium fluoride plant investment, approved in Q1FY27, is a separate diversification project. Q1FY27 Financials: Stronger Revenue, but No Green-Ammonia Earnings Yet PPL reported consolidated revenue from operations of ₹6,124.3 crore in Q1FY27, up 36% year on year and 30.2% quarter on quarter. Profit after tax (PAT) increased 24% year on year to ₹393.2 crore from ₹317.2 crore in Q1FY26, and more than doubled from ₹161.1 crore in Q4FY26. Total fertiliser sales reached 985,143 tonnes, up 4% year on year. ALSO READRs 22 lakh-crore global green hydrogen boom: 3 stocks eyeing India’s 5 MTPA goal These figures provide context for the scale of the existing business and its current operating performance. The stock has jumped about 18% in six months but is still down more than 19% in a year. Its price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio was approximately 13.8. In its 31 July 2026 report, Prabhudas Lilladher maintained an Accumulate rating with a target price of ₹158, valuing PPL at 13 times estimated FY28 earnings per share. This implies 9.53% upside from ₹144.26. The brokerage's target is a broader stock valuation, not a valuation of PPL's green-ammonia allocation. #2 Coromandel International: The Crop-Nutrition Leader With the Largest Disclosed Allocation Among the Three Coromandel International manufactures phosphatic and NPK fertilisers and operates across crop protection, speciality nutrients, organic fertilisers and agri-retail. docs.title: Rs 40,000 cr+ orders for BHEL alone: 5 stocks riding India’s thermal power expansion
docs.text: India could be heading towards a much larger thermal power expansion than previously planned. On 13 October, the Central Electricity Authority (CEA) indicated that India could need an additional 105–150 GW of coal-based power capacity by 2035, compared with its earlier estimate of 97 GW. Rising electricity demand and weaker hydropower generation are increasing dependence on thermal power. The need for reliable, round-the-clock electricity supply is also keeping thermal capacity expansion in focus. This potential expansion could create fresh opportunities for companies manufacturing boilers, turbines, pumps and other thermal power equipment. Engineering and construction contractors could also benefit from new project orders. However, not every company associated with thermal power is equally positioned to benefit from new capacity additions. FE Stock Insights on WhatsApPGet instant alerts on high-conviction investment themes and fundamental deep dives—direct from Financial Express.Join now Why a 150-GW Coal Target Doesn't Guarantee Easy Profits To identify companies positioned to benefit from this expansion, we examined 10 listed companies with exposure to the thermal power sector. Our assessment focused on three criteria: direct involvement in new thermal power projects, orders secured during FY25–FY27, and the financial significance of those orders. Five companies stood out with quantifiable orders linked to thermal power projects. These orders provide greater visibility into their participation in India's potential capacity expansion. However, securing orders does not guarantee profitability. Project execution, cost management and timely completion will determine how effectively these opportunities translate into earnings. Let's take a closer look at these five companies and their role in India's next thermal power expansion. #1 BHEL: Rs 13,500 Crore+ Thermal Order Strengthens Power Expansion Pipeline Bharat Heavy Electricals (BHEL) manufactures boilers, turbines, generators and other equipment for thermal power plants. It also undertakes complete engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) contracts, giving it direct exposure to new coal-based capacity additions. In March 2026, BHEL secured an order worth over Rs 13,500 crore from NTPC for the 3x800 MW Telangana Stage-II thermal power project. The contract covers equipment supply, civil works, installation and commissioning. Completion is scheduled within 62 months from the order award. How a 57% Thermal Market Share Is Driving BHEL’s ₹2.57 Lakh Crore Order Book According to its FY26 annual report, BHEL secured over Rs 40,000 crore in coal-based thermal orders during FY26, representing approximately 57% market share. The company also added 5,180 MW of domestic thermal utility capacity during the year. On 14 October, BHEL's board approved a Rs 500 crore investment to expand manufacturing facilities for thermal and nuclear power sets at its Haridwar unit. In FY26, revenue from operations increased 19.2% YoY to Rs 33,782 crore, while net profit rose 207.6% YoY to Rs 1,578 crore. Higher project execution and improved operating performance supported growth. BHEL's Q2 FY27 results showed revenue rising 24% YoY to Rs 9,300 crore, while net profit increased 120% YoY to Rs 810 crore. EBITDA grew 69% to Rs 1,286 crore. The quarter also saw the addition of 660 MW capacity at Unit 1 of the Udangudi thermal project in Tamil Nadu. BHEL's outstanding order book reached Rs 2,57,571 crore as of September 2026, up 17.3% YoY. However, executing large thermal contracts requires substantial working capital and timely project delivery. Cost overruns, supply disruptions and execution delays remain key risks despite the growing order book. These capabilities allow L&T to execute large ultra-supercritical thermal projects. According to its FY26 annual report, L&T secured orders for multiple 800 MW ultra-supercritical projects in Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh. It also achieved commercial operations at the first unit of the Buxar project and the second unit of the Khurja project. Inside L&T’s ₹62,000 Crore CarbonLite Order Book—And Why Clearances Matter In July 2026, L&T secured a Rs 10,000–15,000 crore order mandate for NTPC's 1,600 MW Lara Stage-III project in Chhattisgarh. This was followed by another Rs 5,000–10,000 crore mandate for the 1,600 MW Chandrapura project in Jharkhand on 7 October. Both projects await environmental clearances before full notices to proceed. The company's July earnings call indicated that CarbonLite Solutions had an order book of approximately Rs 62,000 crore, with another Rs 70,000 crore in order prospects for the remaining FY27 period. docs.title: IDBI Bank shares down 7%: Cabinet approves 60.7% stake sale to Fairfax; brokerages positive
docs.text: The IDBI Bank share price will be in focus today, October 15, after the government decided to sell its stake in the lender. Global investment bank Jefferies sees the move as positive. The share price of IDBI Bank plunged 7% in early trade today. The Union Cabinet on Wednesday, October 14 approved the sale of a 60.72% stake in IDBI Bank to Canada Inc, an entity of Fairfax Financial Holdings, for Rs 52,878 crore. IDBI Bank: Cabinet approves stake sale The government will sell 30.48% stake and the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) will divest 30.24%, according to the Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM). Fairfax will pay Rs 81 per share, a discount of 10% to the closing price of Wednesday, for the entire 60.72% stake in IDBI Bank. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said there were two interested parties who had submitted bids to buy the stake. ALSO READ25%+ sales growth: 2 auto ancillary stocks eyeing more revenue from every vehicle The government will retain a 15% stake in IDBI Bank following the proposed transaction, and LIC will hold 19% stake. This takes their combined holding to 34%. The share purchase agreement is expected to be signed and executed before the end of 2026, the DIPAM secretary said. Under the agreement, the buyer’s invested capital will remain locked in for three years. IDBI Bank will also retain its existing brand name following the transaction, the secretary added. The Fairfax Group owns 40% stake in CSB Bank, 14% in IIFL, and around 57% in Go Digit General Insurance. Jefferies on IDBI Bank deal Global investment bank Jefferies said in a report, “The divestment of stake in IDBI has been in the works since 2021, so its consummation is a positive.” It added that any development around a merger with CSB Bank will be key to watch, especially as CSB has a 1.2% return on assets and a 13% return on equity. IDBI Bank had 1.2% market share in banking-sector loans and 1.3% in deposits as on March, but its profitability was lower. It had a 2.2% return on assets and 15% return on equity in FY26. Its current account savings account (CASA) ratio of 45% is higher than the sector, and the balance sheet has been cleaned up with a gross non-performing loan ratio of 2.3% and a net non-performing loan ratio of 0.2%. ALSO READAditya Birla Capital set for 24% upside? Why Jefferies is bullish amid rising rates “.the Indian financial sector continues to see a change of faces, with new investors and/ or new CEOs. These include change of management at HDFC Bank, Kotak Bank, IndusInd Bank and new strategic investors at RBL Bank, Shriram Finance, IDBI Bank among others. This will keep attrition level in the industry relatively high and may keep their competitive positioning quite dynamic,” Jefferies said. docs.title: Nestlé, HDB to IDBI: 6 stocks plunge as much as 10% despite blockbuster market rally
docs.text: Bulls have taken over Dalal Street today, October 15, as the information technology sector witnessed a buying frenzy. The Nifty has soared above 23,000 points after two weeks and the Sensex is leading with 1,400 points. However, several stocks have bucked the trend as earnings and other factors weighed down sentiment. Here are the six stocks that have slumped in today’s bull-market. Nestle India The Nestle India share price dropped as much as 9% intraday today, before paring some of the losses. The shares plunged after its management flagged concerns about rising inflation. ALSO READ25%+ sales growth: 2 auto ancillary stocks eyeing more revenue from every vehicle Nestlé India on Thursday reported a 36.3% increase in net profit for the July to September quarter. Total sales rose 20.5%, which the company said was driven by double-digit volume growth across its product groups. Manish Tiwary, Chairman and Managing Director said that rising inflation, particularly food inflation, “is a reality”. HDB Financial Services The HDB Financial share price plunged nearly 8% after its net profit for the second quarter of financial year 2027 (Q2FY27) missed the Street’s expectations. Several brokerage also cut their target price on the stock such as Nirmal Bang and Emkay Global. IDBI Bank The IDBI Bank share price tumbled nearly 8% intraday today after the Union Cabinet approved the sale of a 60.72% stake in IDBI Bank to Canada Inc, an entity of Fairfax Financial Holdings, for Rs 52,878 crore. The government will sell a 30.48% stake and the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) will divest 30.24%. Global investment bank Jefferies sees the move as positive. Canara Bank The Canara Bank share price slumped over 6%, mirroring weakness in other public sector banks. The Nifty PSU Bank Index was down 1.3% today. The lender reported an 8.4% year-on-year rise in net profit to Rs 5,175 crore for Q2FY27,supported by improvement in asset quality and core income growth. Its net interest margin for the quarter improved to 2.55% from 2.52% in the previous quarter. Aditya Infotech The share price of Aditya Infotech plunged nearly 10% intraday today, before paring some of the losses. However, the sock has gained over 9% in the last three months and around 96% in the last six months. ALSO READIDBI Bank shares down 7%: Cabinet approves 60.7% stake sale to Fairfax; brokerages positive Emmvee Photovoltaic Power The Emmvee Photovoltaic Power share price plummeted around 8% in early trade today, before paring nearly half of the losses. The company’s net profit and revenue for Q2FY27 rose year-on-year. However, its revenue missed the Street’s estimates. The stock has declined 16% in the last three months but gained 10% in the last six months. docs.title: 25%+ sales growth: 2 auto ancillary stocks eyeing more revenue from every vehicle
docs.text: You may have noticed how the placement of headlights has changed in modern cars. In many models, the main headlamps now sit just above the bumper, while slimmer LED daytime running lights (DRLs) occupy the space higher up, near the bonnet. This is more than a design change. Signature lighting has become a way for automakers to distinguish premium models, while LED technology is gradually replacing conventional halogen lamps. The result is a rise in the value of lighting fitted to each vehicle, creating an opportunity for suppliers to grow even without a sharp increase in vehicle sales. India’s automotive lighting market is expected to grow from about $1.83 billion in 2026 to $2.44 billion by 2031, according to Mordor Intelligence, implying annual growth of 5.9%. But the bigger opportunity lies in the changing product mix. As cars get more sophisticated lighting systems, suppliers can earn more from each vehicle. FE Stock Insights on WhatsApPGet instant alerts on high-conviction investment themes and fundamental deep dives—direct from Financial Express.Join now A Slow-growing Market, a Fast-changing Product Mix Two forces are shaping the automotive lighting opportunity: premiumisation and rising vehicle production. As LEDs replace halogen lamps and automakers adopt more sophisticated lighting systems, the value of lighting fitted to each vehicle increases. This shift in product mix could drive growth even if vehicle production slows. Production growth provides an additional tailwind. India’s automobile industry produced a record 96.9 lakh units in Q1FY27, up 22% YoY, according to figures cited on Uno Minda’s earnings call. The momentum continued into Q2FY27. Maruti reported a 26.4% increase in sales to 6.96 lakh units, while Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles recorded a 40% YoY jump in domestic sales to 2.01 lakh units. Tighter Safety Standards Regulations are also shifting lighting design and performance. Automobile Research Association of India has been harmonizing the lighting standards. AIS-198 and AIS-199 are harmonized with UN regulations and global standards. These standards are mainly focused on safety and compliance, pushing car manufacturers toward better lighting technology. This provides an opportunity for component manufacturers to add value to lighting systems supplied per vehicle. Lumax Industries and UNO Minda offer the most direct exposure to play this shift. Both are positioned to benefit from the transition to LED lighting and rising demand for premium lighting systems. Neolite ZKW Lightings, another player in the segment, has received SEBI approval for its proposed ₹600 crore IPO, although the IPO dates have not been finalised. Lumax Industries: The Direct Play on LED Adoption LED lighting continues to be one of the key growth drivers for Lumax. The company reported a record consolidated revenue of ₹4,184 crore for FY26, up 23% YoY. LED products accounted for 61% of those sales, versus 58% a year ago. The trend continued in Q1FY27, with revenue growing 32.6% to ₹1,223 crore, with LED products contributing 63% of the total sales. Earnings Before Interest, Tax, Depreciation, and Amortisation (EBITDA) margin remained stable at 9.2% for the period. Lumax Industries: Financial Performance PeriodQ1FY26Q1FY27YoY Change (%)Revenue from Operations (₹ crore)922.51,223.232.6%EBITDA (₹ crore)84.50113.0033.7%EBITDA Margin (%)9.20%9.20%No ChangeNet Profit (₹ crore)36.251.141.2% Source: Company Presentation The Order Book & Content Per Vehicle Potential The order book at the end of Q1FY27 stood at ₹2,500 crore, up from ₹2,200 crore at the end of FY26. The order book breakdown offers a glimpse of where growth could come from next. Nearly 90% of the order book comprises LED-based products. ALSO READOnly 1 public charger for every 235 EVs: 2 stocks taking on India’s EV bottleneck Management expects this shift could help them to grow revenue by 15-20% annually over the next three to five years, targeting more than ₹9,000 crore by FY31. Higher content per vehicle (CPV) and vehicle volumes will be key to achieving this target. Lumax expects its lighting content per passenger vehicle to rise from ₹15,000-20,000 currently to ₹22,000-25,000 over the next four to five years. At the midpoint, that represents an increase of about 34%. Lumax Industries: Order Book Composition Source: Company Presentation The Tooling Catalyst Another factor could influence Lumax’s near-term revenue and margins: tooling. As automakers introduce new models and facelifts, suppliers must develop customised moulds and specialised equipment to manufacture components for those vehicles. Shorter design cycles can therefore create recurring tooling opportunities. Management expects mould sales to rise to ₹250-300 crore in FY27, up from ₹180-185 crore in FY26, with most of the revenue expected in the second half of the financial year. This could provide meaningful lift to the margin. The Margin Question Management is targeting an EBITDA margin of 10.5- 11% in FY27, and more than 13% over the next three to four years. The expected growth in tooling revenue in the second half is one part of the near-term recovery. In the long term, the company is focusing on increasing localisation of electronic components, including printed circuit boards (PCBs) used in automotive lighting, which management expected to add 70- 90 bps to margins. The gap between the current 9.2% margin and the long-term target of more than 13% is substantial. Lumax’s rising LED mix and order book provide a foundation for growth. But the key metric to watch is whether margins begin to improve alongside sales, and whether the improvement persists beyond the timing-related boost from tooling. docs.title: Nykaa, Tata Consumer, Blue Star shares: Top stocks to buy | What Kotak Neo suggests - Target price, stop loss
docs.text: Top stocks to buy for short term: Market benchmarks, the Sensex and the Nifty 50, surged up to 2% in intraday deals on Thursday, 15 October, due to buying in select blue-chip stocks amid a selloff in global AI stocks and the healthy start of Q2 earnings of India Inc.According to Amol Athawale, VP - Technical Research, Kotak Neo, 22,500 and 22,450 will continue to act as crucial support levels for the Nifty 50, and as long as the index sustains above these levels, the ongoing pullback may remain intact.On the upside, a decisive breakout above 22,800 could drive the market toward 23,000. Conversely, a decline below 22,450 would weaken the prevailing uptrend, prompting traders to consider exiting their long positions, said Athawale.Stock picks for short term:Amol Athawale recommends buying the following three stocks for the next 1-2 weeks:FSN E-Commerce Ventures (Nykaa) | Previous close: ₹336.50 | Target price: ₹360 | Stop loss: ₹323Athawale highlighted that after the remarkable up move, the stock is taking a breather after many sessions.The consolidation structure suggests bullish continuation chart formation. Additionally, the stock comfortably closed above its short-term moving average."It is likely to resume its uptrend from the current levels in the coming horizon. For positional traders, ₹323 would be the decisive level. If trading above the same, the formation will continue till ₹360. However, if it closes below ₹323, traders may prefer to exit long positions," said Athawale.Tata Consumer Products | Previous close: ₹987.90 | Target price: ₹1,040 | Stop loss: ₹960Athawale said that after its declining trend, the stock reversed from its important support zone.It has formed a rounding bottom chart pattern on the daily scale, and it is in a steady uptrend.The technical indicator like RSI is also indicating a further uptrend from current levels, which could boost the bullish momentum in the coming horizon."As long as the stock is trading above ₹960, the bullish trend is likely to continue. Above which, the stock could move up to ₹1,040," said Athawale.Blue Star | Previous close: ₹1,614 | Target price: ₹1,730 | Stop loss: ₹1,555Athawale underscored that on the daily timeframe, post reversal from its support zone, the stock is in a rising channel chart structure showing a higher highs and higher lows sequence pattern.Moreover, the technical indicator RSI is also suggesting a further upward trend from present levels, which may enhance the bullish momentum in the near term."For the upcoming few trading sessions, ₹1,555 may act as the trend-deciding level for the bulls; if it holds above this level, we can expect further uptrend toward ₹1,730," said Athawale.Read all market-related news hereDisclaimer: This article is for educational purposes only and does not constitute investment advice. The views and recommendations expressed are those of the individual expert, not Mint. We advise investors to consult with certified experts before making any investment decisions, as market conditions can change rapidly and circumstances may vary.

docs.title: Buy Motherson Wiring Ltd for the Target Rs.41 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
Demand remains strong; margins set to bottom soon 
Motherson Wiring (MSWIL) has corrected ~25% over the past year, driven primarily by margin pressure rather than any deterioration in its growth outlook. Elevated copper prices and a lag in customer pass-through, a slower-thanexpected ramp-up of greenfield facilities, and the minimum-wage hike in the NCR region have been the key drivers of margin contraction. We believe these headwinds are largely transitory. Despite rising copper prices, the catch-up in cost pass-through should support margins, while improving utilization at greenfield facilities should drive a recovery in profitability through 2HFY27. The medium-to-long-term thesis remains unchanged. MSWIL has consistently outgrown underlying passenger-vehicle production, supported by its marketleading position in India’s wiring harness industry, deep relationships with leading OEMs, and strong execution capabilities. Growth remains underpinned by rising content per vehicle (premiumization, electrification, and increasing feature complexity), higher EV penetration, localization opportunities, deeper participation across existing customer platforms, and continued new model launches by OEMs. MSWIL also enjoys strong capital efficiency, with management maintaining a >40% RoCE objective and the company having historically delivered returns above this threshold. Given its competitive positioning, top-decile capital efficiency, and the benefits of EVs and other megatrends in autos, we believe MSWIL deserves the rich valuations it commands, and the correction offers a more attractive entry point. We reiterate our BUY rating with a TP of INR41 (based on 35x FY28E EPS).
* MSWIL’s growth outlook is supported by a combination of near-term capacity ramp-up, deeper participation across existing OEM platforms, and structurally rising electrical and electronic content per vehicle.
* In the near term, the ramp-up of greenfield facilities at Navagam, Kharkhoda, and Pune, alongside the commencement of new customer programs, should remain important growth drivers. The three facilities generated INR10.4b of revenue in FY26, while management has indicated combined annualized revenue potential of around INR20–21b, subject to customer production schedules and volume ramp-up (1QFY27 revenue stood at INR4.5b). As of 1QFY27, utilization stood at ~80% at Kharkhoda, ~60% at Navagam, and ~50% at Pune, with the latter affected by customer volumes falling short of initial forecasts. This leaves meaningful headroom for revenue growth from capacity that has already been commissioned.
* Alongside capacity ramp-up, MSWIL continues to benefit from new model launches, premiumization, and deeper participation with existing OEM customers. The company’s long-standing relationships and technological capabilities have led customers to entrust it with more platforms, higher content, and greater responsibility, supporting growth ahead of underlying industry volumes
* The more structural growth driver, however, is the increasing electrical and electronic content per vehicle, which should enable wiring-harness demand to grow faster than underlying vehicle production over time. Premiumization, connected-car features, infotainment, electronically controlled safety systems, sensors, cameras, and ADAS are increasing the number and complexity of electrical and data connections within vehicles, thus increasing the content per vehicle over time.
* MSWIL is positioning itself for this transition through a powertrain-agnostic portfolio spanning ICE, EV, hybrid, and CNG platforms. Its capabilities extend across low- and high-voltage harnesses, while the company is also expanding into high-voltage, dual-voltage and integrated harness systems, and charging and power-electronics solutions.
* Backed by the ramp-up of greenfield facilities and incremental order wins from the model launch pipeline of OEMs over the next two years, we expect MSWIL to record a 17% revenue CAGR over FY26-28. For FY27, we currently factor in a 20% revenue growth (below the company’s guidance of over 24%)
* MSWIL offers a pure play on the Indian automotive market (>95% of revenue from India). With over 40% market share, the company enjoys a market leadership position in the Indian wiring harness industry, with strong headroom for a sustainable increase in content, benefiting from mega trends witnessed in the automotive industry (premiumization, electrification, connected vehicles, etc.).
* The company enjoys healthy returns, led by superior efficiencies and economies of scale, healthy margins, higher asset turnover, and lower capex requirements. These parameters reflect high capital efficiencies and superior cash-flow generation.
* With copper prices now stabilizing, we do expect margins to gradually normalize in the coming quarters as the benefit of price pass-through will be reflected in financials. Overall, we estimate MSWIL to post a CAGR of 17%/13%/12% in revenue/EBITDA/PAT over FY26-28. The company’s premium valuations at 36x/28x FY27E/FY28E EPS seem justified, given its strong competitive positioning, top-decile capital efficiency, and benefits of EVs and other mega trends in autos. We reiterate our BUY rating with a TP of INR41 (based on 35x FY28E EPS

docs.title: Buy Canara Bank Ltd for the Target Rs.160 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
Healthy performance; margin improves 3bp QoQ Lower provisioning and reduced opex drive earnings beat 
* Canara Bank (CBK) posted a 2QFY27 standalone PAT of INR51.7b (up 8% YoY/7% QoQ; 8% beat on MOFSLe), fueled by lower-than-expected provisions and opex.
* NII grew 20% YoY/8% QoQ to INR110.0b (3% higher than MOFSLe). CBK’s NIM improved 3bp QoQ to 2.55% (in line). The bank maintained its NIM guidance of 2.5-2.6% for FY27.
* The bank’s loan book grew 20% YoY/7% QoQ to INR13.6t. Deposits grew 13% YoY/ 5% QoQ to INR16.97t.
* Slippages stood at INR19b (INR18b in 1QFY27). GNPA/NNPA ratios improved 24bp/6bp QoQ to 1.33%/ 0.30%. PCR rose to 77.9% (up 71bp QoQ). The impact of the ECL transition is likely to be in the range of INR120- 150b (vs. INR100-120b earlier) and is likely to affect CRAR by ~1.0-1.2%.
* We tweak our estimates for FY27E/28E and expect CBK to deliver an FY27 RoA/RoE of 1.06%/18.9%. Reiterate BUY with a TP of INR160 (based on 1.1x Mar’28E ABV+ INR13 for subsidiaries).
 Business growth steady; asset quality ratios improve 
* CBK’s 2QFY27 PAT grew 8% YoY/7% QoQ to INR51.7b (8% above MOFSLe), aided by lower-than-expected provisioning and opex.
* NII grew 20% YoY/8% QoQ to INR110.0b (~3% beat). Its margin expanded 3bp QoQ to 2.55% (in line). CBK retained its FY27 NIM guidance at 2.5-2.6%.
* Other income declined 18% YoY/ 14% QoQ to INR57.7b (3% lower than MOFSLe) with lower PSLC and treasury income. Total revenue thus rose 4% YoY to INR167.8b (in line).
* Operating expenses increased 5% YoY (down 3% QoQ) to INR80.2b (4% lower than MOFSLe). C/I ratio declined to 47.8% (vs. 49.0% in 1QFY27). PPoP thus rose 2% YoY/1% QoQ to INR87.4b (5% beat).
* The loan book grew 20.4% YoY/6.5% QoQ, led by robust growth in the retail (21% YoY/6.2% QoQ) and Agri segments (14.3% YoY/10.2% QoQ). The gold loan book stood at INR2.8t, of which the agricultural gold loan book accounted for INR1.7t.
* Deposits grew 13.1% YoY/5.3% QoQ to INR16.97t. CASA deposits grew 4.9% YoY/2.6% QoQ. CASA ratio stood at 29.0% (vs 29.7% in 1QFY27), while the CD ratio increased to 80.2% (vs. 79.3% in 1QFY27).
* Provisions came in at INR17.8b (13% below MOFSLe), down 14% QoQ and 24% YoY. Slippages increased marginally to INR19b (INR18b in 1QFY27), even as asset quality ratios improved across segments. GNPA/NNPA ratios improved 24bp/6bp QoQ to 1.33%/0.30%. PCR stood at 77.9%.
* Reported credit costs dipped to 0.47% from 0.49% in 1QFY27. SMA book (INR50m and above) declined to 0.51% from 0.58% in 1QFY27.
 Valuation and view: Reiterate BUY with a TP of INR160 
CBK reported a steady quarter with an uptick in margins and lower provisions and opex while asset quality continued to improve. CBK’s NIM is expected to be rangebound at 2.5-2.6% for FY27 aided by rate hikes. Loan growth was healthy and broadbased with RAM segments leading the overall growth. Deposit growth lagged credit growth, while CBK remains focused on improving the granularity of deposits. CBK maintains its loan growth guidance of 11-12%. The bank’s asset quality improved, with lower NPAs across asset classes. CBK will need to make additional provisions of INR120-150b for the ECL transition, with an estimated impact of 1.0-1.2% on CRAR. The RoA guidance stands at 1%+ for FY27. We marginally tweak our estimates for FY27E/28E and expect CBK to deliver FY27E RoA/RoE of 1.06%/18.9%. Reiterate BUY with a TP of INR160 (based on 1.1x Mar’28E ABV+ INR13 for subsidiaries).

docs.text:
Strong operating performance drives 11% PAT beat 
* Billionbrains Garage Ventures’ (GROWW) operating revenue of INR15b in 2QFY27 grew 47% YoY (5% beat). For 1HFY27, revenue grew 56% YoY.
* Operating expenses rose 29% YoY in 2QFY27 to INR5.3b (6% below est.), with employee expenses rising 36% YoY (11% below est.) and other expenses rising 25% YoY (in line). EBITDA grew 60% YoY to INR9.7b, reflecting EBITDA margin of 64.5% (59.2% in 2QFY26 and MOFSLe of 60.4%).
* PAT for the quarter came in at INR7.2b, growing 54% YoY (reflecting an 11% beat on our estimates). For 1HFY27, PAT grew 72% YoY.
* The impact of SEBI’s proposed optionality measures on CAS is expected to be limited, with derivatives activity likely to normalize relatively quickly following implementation, according to management.
* We have increased our earnings estimates by 4%/1% for FY27/28, considering strong 2QFY27 performance driven by improved operational efficiency. We reiterate our BUY rating with a TP of INR240 (premised on 38x FY28E EPS).
 MTF surge supporting broking revenue/order improvement 
* Broking revenue rose 29% YoY to INR10.5b, driven by 24% YoY growth in orders to 517.3m as well as an increase in revenue per order to INR20.4 (INR19.7 in 2QFY26).
* Derivatives revenue grew 13% YoY but declined 14% QoQ to ~INR6.9b, owing to market adjustments to CAS. GROWW’s retail options premium ADTO market share was 11.0%, up from 8.7% in 2QFY26.
* Cash revenue grew 29% YoY/8% QoQ to ~INR2.7b, with ADTO market share at 15.4% (12.9% in 2QFY26). Cash orders witnessed ~3% sequential growth, while revenue/order continues to benefit from rising MTF adoption.
* Commodity derivatives benefited from growth in user adoption and industry momentum, with revenue growing 26% QoQ and contributing 6% to GROWW’s total operating revenue. Launched in 3QFY26, commodity derivatives currently have 505,000 active users.
* MTF revenue grew 26% QoQ to INR1.6b (INR503m in 2QFY26), with the MTF book scaling to INR43.5b by the end of 2QFY27 (INR37.7b in 1QFY27), reflecting a stable market share of 2.7%. Management expects quarterly book additions of INR6-7b to continue, supported by ongoing improvements in risk control.
* The credit segment’s revenue rose 37% YoY/7% QoQ to INR909m. Disbursement by partners declined sequentially to INR3.5b, with ~96% being unsecured in nature. Groww Creditserv’s unsecured loan book increased sequentially to INR13.8b (INR13b in 1QFY27), while the secured loan book continues to scale significantly at INR4.1b (INR3.1b in 1QFY27).
* The AMC’s AUM reached INR72b, with revenue of INR41.3m and an operating loss of INR83m during the quarter
* Wealth management AUM crossed INR100b to INR108b in 2QFY27 (INR98b in 1QFY27), with active users increasing meaningfully from 421,000+ to 607,000+, driven by rising adoption of MF Prime.
* Cost-to-grow declined sequentially to ~INR1.1b (INR1.5b in 1QFY27), primarily due to the impact of IPL-related spending in the last quarter. The transacting user base reached 24.1m by the end of 2QFY27. With a recovery in market, the quarterly run rate is expected to normalize at INR1.2-1.3b.
* Cost-to-serve grew 25% YoY to INR2.1b, largely driven by: 1) a higher number of trading days, 2) a rise in AI costs, and 3) a one-time impact of INR100-130m from delayed expiry-day files.
* GROWW continues to report strong revenue growth YoY, driven by rising product adoption by users. Its brokerage business is gaining market share across segments, with its newer products, MTF and commodities, aggressively fueling further growth. The scale, coupled with strong operational efficiency, has also driven robust profitability growth during the quarter.
* We expect overall order volumes in the broking segment to report ~20% growth over FY27-28, backed by market share gains, with revenue growth further supported by improving revenue per order. Continued expansion in the MTF segment, along with gradual growth in LAS and wealth management, is expected to provide an additional boost to top-line growth.
* We have increased our earnings estimates by 4%/1% for FY27/28, considering strong 2QFY27 performance driven by improved operational efficiency. We reiterate our BUY rating with a TP of INR240 (premised on 38x FY28E EPS).

docs.title: Buy Radico Khaitan Ltd for the Target Rs. 5,350 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
Growth catalysts intact; on track for FY27 guidance 
* Radico Khaitan (RDCK) has materially outperformed the IMFL industry by shifting its portfolio toward Prestige & Above (P&A) brands. P&A volumes have increased at a 15% CAGR over FY15-26 to 17m cases in FY26 from 4m in FY15, while the segment’s contribution to RDCK’s IMFL revenue has increased to 70% from less than 40%. With luxury and semi-luxury brands already contributing 10% of revenue (~INR5b), the mix upgrade opportunity remains meaningful. RDCK targets 25% growth in FY27 for its luxury segment. We expect P&A volume growth to remain strong, supported by premiumization, portfolio innovation and further market-share gains.
* Growth outperformance vs. United Spirits (UNSP) and Pernod Ricard underscores RDCK’s superior execution. Over FY19-27E, RDCK’s P&A volumes are expected to expand 3.7x vs. 1.4x for UNSP, while P&A revenue is projected to grow 5x vs. 2x for UNSP. RDCK’s P&A revenue share has consequently increased from 14% of UNSP’s P&A revenue in FY19 to 27% in FY26, and we expect this share to rise to ~30% in FY27E. RDCK expects its FY27 P&A volumes to grow by 25% YoY, reinforcing confidence in near-term momentum.
* State-level policy changes could provide an additional growth catalyst for RDCK’s premium portfolio. Karnataka’s pricing rationalization is supporting P&A portfolio (big MRP cuts for luxury brands such as Rampur and Royal Ranthambore). Progressive policy in UP (accounts for 20-25% of domestic volumes) also provides a strong base to deepen RDCK’s P&A presence. Separately, Maharashtra is showing signs of stabilization after initial disruption; the pressure will be in the base in 2HFY27. The UK and EU FTAs could further support premiumization and improve the growth outlook.
* Margin expansion is the second leg of RDCK’s earnings story. EBITDA margin improved to 16.9% in FY26 from 12% in FY24, and management is targeting 20% in FY27, implying ~350bp expansion. While ENA, glass and packaging costs remain high, premiumization-led mix improvement, operating leverage, backward integration and packaging efficiencies should offset them. Moreover, the India-UK FTA is estimated to drive annual input cost savings of INR700- 750m. We forecast EBITDA margin of 20.4% in FY27E and 21.7% by FY29E.
* The improving earnings profile is also supporting balance-sheet deleveraging. Net debt declined by INR1.38b from Mar’26 to INR1.06b as of Jun’26, with management targeting a net debt-free balance sheet in FY27. We expect APAT to increase from INR6.1b in FY26 to INR13.4b in FY29E, implying a ~30% CAGR, driven by P&A growth, supportive policies and margin expansion.
* RDCK trades at 55x/45x FY28E/FY29E EPS, and the projected earnings trajectory supports a premium valuation. We value the company at 55x 2,000 Sep’28E EPS to arrive at a target price of INR5,350 and maintain BUY.
 Increasing market share with more focus on P&A 
* RDCK recorded 20m cases in 2015, while the IMFL industry recorded 325m cases. In FY26, the IMFL industry clocked 430m cases, and RDCK scaled up to 38m cases (9% share). However, P&A volumes reached ~17m cases in FY26 from 4m cases in FY15.
* RDCK has been consistently delivering industry-leading volume and revenue growth. The shift from the popular portfolio to the premium portfolio (P&A) has been driving strong growth outperformance. P&A volumes have compounded ~15% over FY15-26, contributing 44% of IMFL volumes (vs. 20% in FY15). Similarly, P&A revenue contribution has jumped to ~70% of IMFL revenue from less than 40% in FY15. The premiumization play book of mid-premium has been replicated in multiple luxury/semi-luxury brands, reflecting the company’s superior execution capabilities and longevity of strong growth. Luxury/semiluxury brands now contribute ~10% of revenue (~INR5b in FY26), providing a further runway for mix-led growth.
* Furthermore, RDCK raised its FY27 P&A volume growth guidance to over 25% (vs. earlier 20%), reflecting strong momentum in the premium portfolio. There is still enough headroom for RDCK to keep leveraging its execution to gain share, particularly in whiskey (P&A).
* RDCK continues to deliver strong growth in its P&A segment, with premiumization remaining a key structural driver. The luxury and semi-luxury portfolios continue to grow at a healthy pace, supported by new launches and rising consumer demand.
* Management remains committed to steadily reducing its debt, supported by healthy free cash flow generation. Net debt declined by INR1.38b since Mar'26, and net debt stood at INR1.06b as of Jun’26. Management is targeting a net debt-free balance sheet in FY27.
* RDCK remains focused on accelerating growth in the premium and luxury segments while driving greater efficiency across operations with disciplined capital allocation.
* Its P&A sales stood ~15% of UNSP’s P&A sales in FY19, which have now grown to ~30% (as of FY26), and we expect this share to further improve going forward. The valuation gap with UNSP has narrowed significantly, reflecting market recognition of RDCK’s brand strength and execution.
* RDCK is currently trading at 55x/45x FY28E/FY29E EPS, with RoE/RoIC of 23%/29% in FY28E. We believe a ~30% EPS CAGR over FY26-29E provides adequate support for sustaining rich valuations. We value the company at 55x P/E on Sep’28E EPS to derive a TP of INR5,350.

docs.title: Buy The Leela Palaces Ltd For Target Rs.720 by Choice Institutional Equities
docs.text:
Pricing Strength Drives Robust Q2FY27 Performance 
THELEELA delivered a strong operational performance in Q2FY27, with RevPAR growing 30% YoY to INR 17,225, primarily driven by a 30% increase in ARR to INR 25,046. The BRICS Summit in Delhi and a shift towards premium room categories supported pricing, with suite occupancy rising by over 700 bps YoY. City hotels remained the key growth driver, with H1FY27 RevPAR increasing 26% YoY to INR 15,948 and occupancy improving to 74%. Resorts reported 18% RevPAR growth to INR 14,722, although Coorg’s ramp-up continued to weigh on occupancy; ex-Coorg occupancy was close to 60%. We remain positive on H2FY27, supported by the upcoming festive, wedding season and continued strength in luxury demand
We raise our RevPAR and ARR estimate owing to
a) Strong outperformance in a seasonally weak quarter
c) Event-led demand. We now expect FY28E EBITDA margin to come in higher than FY27E by ~103 bps, leading to an estimate revision of 17.5% for FY28E EBITDA. Further, H2FY27E is expected to be stronger and we remain positive on THELEEELA’s prospects. We believe THELEELA merits a higher multiple of 22.0x FY28E EV/Adj. EBITDA (vs. 18.0x earlier) owing to strong ARR outperformance and brand value. We, therefore, rate the stock a ‘BUY’ and raise our TP to INR 720/share (vs. INR 540). Our DCF-derived valuation of INR 700/share provides a sanity check.
As per the latest shareholding pattern of Jun’26: Creation of direct pledge of ~73.6% of promoter shareholding for “Payments or distributions to the investors of the Promoters, repayment of shareholder loans of the Promoters…”
 Revenue Beats Estimate by 11%; EBITDA Grows 36% YoY 
* RevPAR stood at INR 17,255, a ~30% increase YoY, entirely driven by ARR growth of 30%, while occupancy remained flat YoY at 69.0%
* Revenue came in at INR 4.1 Bn for Q2FY27, an improvement of 32.6% YoY (beating CIE estimate by 11%)
* EBIDTA stood at INR 1.8 Bn, increase of 36.1% YoY. EBITDA margin improved by 119 bps to 45.6% (versus CIE estimate of 46.3%)
* PAT came in at INR 946 Mn with PAT margin for Q2FY27 standing at 23.0% versus CIE estimate of 22.0%
 Pipeline Expansion Sustains Long-term Growth Visibility 
THELEELA has 1,038 keys under development across 10 properties, with openings planned through CY30E. Jaisalmer and the 63-key Waterstones property in Mumbai are targeted to open in FY27E, while civil work is progressing at Srinagar and Bandhavgarh. The 100-key Ayodhya project has reached the shell-and-core stage; the company has proposed to invest up to INR 1,850 Mn through CCPS to fund the project’s development and working capital requirement. At Agra, piling work has been completed, while design and site preparation are underway for the 30-key Tadoba resort and the 250-key BKC Mumbai hotel.
